title: Mplus Market Pulse - 07 Oct 2026
body: MY: Tracking positive regional performance, the local bourse continued to trade higher ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement. Market breadth turned positive, with 667 gainers against 456 losers. Sector-wise, both Technology and Healthcare outperformed with gains exceeding 3%, while Financial Services lagged the most. US: Wall Street logged solid gains with the Dow rising 0.5%, the S&P 500 gaining 0.6% to reach new record highs, and the Nasdaq jumping 0.5% higher as US 10-year Treasury yields slipped to 5.3%, while Brent crude hovered at USD100/bbl amid potential Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. US: Wall Street may retain its constructive tone after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs, helped by easing Treasury yields and stabilising oil prices. AI remains a key earnings driver, with Marvell (MRVL) in focus after raising its FY2028 revenue target to USD20.0bn and guiding FY2031 revenue to USD70.0- 90.0bn, underpinned by strong demand for custom AI silicon and optical connectivity. Meanwhile, Salesforce (CRM) could benefit from renewed strength in enterprise software as concerns over AI disruption ease, while Meta (META) continues expanding its AI offerings to businesses through its Meta Enterprise Platform. MY: On the local front, the FBMKLCI is poised to track global tech strength, with sentiment supported by robust earnings and positioning ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 October. The semiconductor and automation space could remain in focus, with semiconductors, AI and high-value investments among the Government's key priorities. UWC stands out after 4QFY26 revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.2m, while net profit surged 129.7%, reflecting stronger semiconductor demand and project execution. VITROX could also attract interest following a sharp improvement in 2QFY26 earnings. Meanwhile, TOPGLOV offers an earnings-driven play after 4QFY26 revenue rose 39.7% to RM1.25bn, with net profit surging 352.6%. Selective buying provided a minor lift to the local bourse on Tuesday, though the benchmark remains capped under key moving averages. Downside risk persists as the MACD histogram stays below zero while the RSI is oversold below 30. Key resistance is pegged at 1,648-1,663, while support is expected around 1,603-1,618. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200m (RM817m). (The Edge) Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. (The Edge) Top Glove Corporation Bhd (TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78bn pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72bn in FY2026. The group's net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63m in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83m in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25bn. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove's net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96m. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23bn as volume grew close to 30%. (The Edge) Samaiden Group Bhd (SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99- megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238m. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. (The Edge) Mesiniaga Bhd (MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. (The Edge) Scientex Bhd (SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580m to boost the property developer's land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. (The Edge) Dialog Group Bhd (DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand's 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. (The Edge) Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (ELRIDGE) is investing RM45m to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45m in cash. (The Edge) Insights Analytics Bhd (IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44m subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. (The Edge) Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm's shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83m shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140m. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. (The Edge) ZenaTech, Inc. (ZENA) advanced its ZenaDrone 2000 heavy-lift autonomous interceptor through prototype assembly in Sharjah, UAE, targeting Q1 2027 flight testing. Built with a 40 kg payload capacity and four-plus hours of hover endurance, the gasoline-powered platform will validate autonomous navigation and multi-target threat pursuit alongside its Interceptor P-1 system. (Investing.com) ONEOK, Inc. (OKE) completed its acquisition of Brazos Midstream's Permian Midland Basin natural gas gathering and processing assets for approximately USD 4.425 billion in cash. The transaction more than doubles ONEOK's Midland Basin processing capacity to roughly 2.3 billion cubic feet per day and adds 600,000 dedicated acres backed by long-term fixed-fee contracts averaging over 12 years. title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Lower as It Tracks Cautious Wall Street Performance
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Thursday, October 1, 2026, under persistent selling pressure across major blue-chip counters, tracking a mixed and cautious overnight performance on Wall Street. The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 20.81 points, or 1.26 per cent, to finish at 1,630.36, down from Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. After opening 1.30 points weaker at 1,649.87, the key index fluctuated between an intraday low of 1,630.10 and a high of 1,649.87 throughout the trading session. Market breadth was negative as decliners outpaced gainers 750 to 342, with 495 counters trading unchanged, 1,186 untraded, and 12 suspended. Total market turnover dropped to 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion, compared to 3.63 billion units worth RM3.62 billion recorded on Wednesday. Economic data released earlier in the day showed that the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) slipped into contraction territory, falling to 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August—marking the first downturn in operating conditions in four months. Regionally, the S&P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI also eased to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. Blue-Chip Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial, utility, and healthcare heavyweights experienced notable selling pressure: - CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. - IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. - Tenaga Nasional lost 6 sen to RM12.90. - Maybank slipped 4 sen to RM9.95. - Public Bank fell 3 sen to RM4.67. In active trading, ACE Market debutant GB Bond slumped 4.5 sen to close at 20.5 sen. Jaks Resources dropped 2.5 sen to 18 sen, and VS Industry dipped 1 sen to 27 sen. Meanwhile, Zetrix AI and HHRG each added half a sen to close at 16.5 sen. title: Bursa Malaysia Key Index Continues Uptrend at Midday
body: Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index maintained its upward trend, increasing by 0.33 percent at midday due to bargain hunting in selected heavyweights. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose by 5.44 points to 1,635.80 from the previous day's close of 1,630.36. The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, fluctuating between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 during the morning trading session. Across the broader market, there were more decliners than gainers, with 507 losers compared to 499 gainers. Additionally, 494 counters remained unchanged, 1,273 were untraded, and 24 were suspended. The market saw a turnover of 2.24 billion shares worth RM1.26 billion. Hong Leong Investment Bank noted that the barometer index might continue its risk-off consolidation amid high oil prices and bond yields. It also highlighted persistent foreign outflows, US-Iran tensions, and a hawkish Federal Reserve stance as factors affecting market sentiment. The bank identified immediate resistance levels at 1,667-1,682, followed by 1,705-1,720. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose by nine sen to RM10.04, Public Bank added four sen to RM4.71, Tenaga Nasional increased 16 sen to RM13.06, and IHH Healthcare expanded by 11 sen to RM7.81. However, CIMB eased by one sen to RM7.68. In active trading, Jaks Resources firmed by half a sen to 18.5 sen, JCY International advanced 10 sen to 65.5 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and Top Glove inched up 3.5 sen to 77 sen, while Zetrix AI decreased 2.5 sen to 14 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries surged 84 sen to RM41.96, UWC gained 36 sen to RM7.46, United Plantations advanced 36 sen to RM31.32, and both Vitrox and UMS Integration climbed 34 sen to RM10.34 and RM8.99, respectively. Kuala Lumpur Kepong led the decliners, falling 46 sen to RM20.96. Other notable decliners included Enra, which lost 29 sen to 69 sen, Allianz Malaysia, which fell 28 sen to RM20.72, BLD Plantations, which shed 26 sen to RM14.74, and Dutch Lady Milk Industries, which erased 20 sen to RM29.80. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 115.75 points to 17,474.73, the FBM Emas Index added 51.08 points to 12,194.61, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 50.09 points to 11,983.24. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 66.45 points to 12,079.46, while the FBM ACE Index improved 6.33 points to 5,489.30. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.99 of a point to 178.72, the Energy Index gained 1.06 points to 836.07, the Financial Services Index rose 55.60 points to 19,116.51, and the Plantation Index increased by 4.58 points to 9,031.15.

title: Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts
body: Oct 23 ruling on bid to restrain RHB from closing Maritime Network's accounts KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): The High Court here on Thursday fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company's bid to restrain RHB Bank Bhd (LK:RHBBANK) from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit. Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank's counsel, Gan Khong Aik. Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts. He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care. Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer is that of debtor and creditor. In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company's application for a full injunction. According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005. On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines. The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines were allegedly breached. The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025. The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application. The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its minimum due diligence guidelines governing foreign-exchange transactions to the company within 45 days. Maritime Network further alleged that the bank's vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself. This conduct, the company asserted, amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights. It also claimed that the bank's conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav
body: KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. Sektor teknologi, tenaga jadi pilihan pelabur asing Walaupun pelabur asing secara keseluruhan mencatatkan jualan bersih, terdapat beberapa sektor yang masih menerima aliran masuk dana. Sektor teknologi menerima aliran masuk asing tertinggi sebanyak RM131 juta, diikuti sektor tenaga sebanyak RM93.2 juta dan pembinaan sebanyak RM78.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM460.6 juta, diikuti utiliti RM339.8 juta dan penjagaan kesihatan RM163.1 juta. Dari sudut saham pula, antara kaunter yang menerima aliran masuk bersih asing tertinggi ialah Gamuda sebanyak RM86.2 juta, Solarvest Holdings RM65.4 juta, Westports Holdings RM55.1 juta dan Southern Cable Group RM53.4 juta. Dalam tempoh sama, Tenaga Nasional Berhad mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM278.1 juta, diikuti Malayan Banking RM159.3 juta dan RHB Bank RM135.9 juta. September turut menyaksikan jualan pelabur asing Trend tersebut turut dapat dilihat sepanjang September apabila pelabur asing menjual bersih saham Malaysia sebanyak RM1.69 bilion. Dalam tempoh sama, institusi tempatan mencatatkan pembelian bersih RM205.7 juta, manakala pelabur runcit membeli bersih RM1.48 bilion. Bagi September, sektor perladangan menjadi penerima aliran masuk asing terbesar sebanyak RM290.6 juta, diikuti tenaga RM230.2 juta serta pengangkutan dan logistik RM204.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak RM1.48 bilion, diikuti utiliti RM642.2 juta dan produk serta perkhidmatan perindustrian RM310.8 juta. Aliran dana Asia kembali negatif Trend jualan asing di Malaysia berlaku ketika pelabur asing secara keseluruhan kembali mengeluarkan dana dari pasaran saham Asia. MBSB Research berkata, kesemua lapan pasaran Asia yang dipantau mencatatkan aliran keluar asing pada minggu berkenaan dengan jumlah keseluruhan AS$10.89 bilion, selepas mencatatkan pembelian bersih pada minggu sebelumnya. Korea Selatan merekodkan aliran keluar terbesar sebanyak AS$6.20 bilion, diikuti India AS$2.91 bilion dan Thailand AS$796.4 juta. Ekonomi Malaysia turut beri isyarat bercampur Dalam perkembangan ekonomi domestik, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian sektor pembuatan Malaysia susut kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, menunjukkan kemerosotan keadaan operasi buat kali pertama sejak Mei 2026. MBSB Research berkata tempahan baharu merosot buat kali pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan, manakala pertumbuhan pengeluaran perlahan ke paras terendah dalam tempoh tujuh bulan. Keyakinan perniagaan turut jatuh ke paras terendah dalam tempoh lima bulan. Pada masa sama, inflasi harga pengeluar Malaysia meningkat 10.7% tahun ke tahun pada Ogos, iaitu peningkatan bagi bulan keenam berturut-turut dan kadar tertinggi sejak Jun 2022. Pasaran global kekal berhati-hati Di Amerika Syarikat, pertumbuhan pekerjaan yang lebih perlahan serta kadar inflasi yang masih melebihi sasaran menimbulkan ketidakpastian terhadap hala tuju dasar monetari negara itu. Dalam tempoh sama, dolar Amerika Syarikat meningkat 0.3% berbanding ringgit kepada RM4.0842, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent turun 2% kepada AS$102.25 setong dan minyak sawit mentah susut 2.9% kepada RM4,535 setan. Weekly Fund Flow-Week Ended 2 O… Secara keseluruhan, laporan MBSB Research menunjukkan Bursa Malaysia masih berdepan tekanan daripada pengeluaran dana asing, namun aktiviti pembelian oleh pelabur tempatan dan runcit membantu mengimbangi sebahagian tekanan tersebut ketika sentimen pelabur serantau turut dipengaruhi oleh perkembangan ekonomi global dan petunjuk ekonomi domestik yang bercampur. - DagangNews.com

title: Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng Ing Yeow downgraded AMMB Holdings, CIMB Group Holdings and RHB Bank to “Hold” from “Buy” in a banking-sector review. He cut their target prices to RM6.70 from RM7.80, RM8.10 from RM8.70 and RM8.00 from RM9.50, respectively. In contrast, he upgraded Public Bank to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised its target price to RM5.30 from RM4.90, naming it his top banking pick for 4Q26. Raymond Ng Ing Yeow is ranked No.10 among 17 financial services analysts on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 66% expert rating, with a 7% average return and a 56% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. The changes come as the yield on 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose to 3.94% on September 25 from 3.60% at end-June. Higher yields reduce the market value of bonds already held by banks, potentially weighing on treasury-related non-interest income before the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields emerges. Raymond said the immediate impact appears manageable, but repeated increases in yields could make earnings less predictable and limit further gains in bank valuations. Under his hypothetical 30-basis-point yield-rise scenario, the estimated gross mark-to-market impact for AMMB Holdings and Bank Islam Malaysia is equivalent to about 10% of their projected annual non-interest income, compared with 4.5% for CIMB Group Holdings and 3.2% for RHB Bank. Public Bank’s direct earnings sensitivity is lower at 1.3%. These are pre-tax estimates that exclude hedging and other offsets—not cuts to earnings forecasts. Raymond said the three downgrades reflect weaker visibility over non-interest income and a higher hurdle for bank-share valuations to rise further. He favours Public Bank for its exceptionally low impaired-loan ratio, resilient earnings and relatively limited direct earnings exposure to the bond-market sell-off, although its bond holdings could still affect book value. He maintained a “Neutral” sector view, noting that foreign investors sold a net RM1.3 billion of Malaysian banking shares between July 1 and September 25, while higher bond yields have made fixed-income investments more competitive. As of 2:09 p.m. on September 29, the Bursa Malaysia Financial Services index dropped 1% to 19,394.6 points. title: RHB Could Face Earnings Pressure From Elevated Bond Yields
body: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on RHB Bank Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM8.00, saying the lender’s earnings outlook remains broadly stable despite pressure on non-interest income from the recent spike in Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields.  Following a recent meeting with RHB Bank’s management, HLIB said weaker trading income is likely to weigh on 3Q26 non-interest income (NOII), with limited time left in the quarter for market conditions to recover.  However, the research house said the impact should be viewed mainly as foregone trading upside rather than significant trading losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book.  Management has also been tactically reducing securities exposure and crystallising gains where possible. HLIB said the outlook for 4Q26 is less negative, as RHB would have more time to reposition its portfolio should bond yields stabilise or decline.  Despite the NOII headwinds, RHB has retained its 10.8% to 11.0% return on equity target, although HLIB believes the group is now more likely to achieve the lower end of that range.  With securities trading becoming a less dependable earnings driver, greater reliance will fall on core operations.  Loan growth remains on track at around 6%, while management has reset cost growth guidance to 1% or below, potentially supporting better operating leverage.  Credit costs are also tracking near the lower end of RHB’s 13 to 14 basis point guidance, with management comfortable at around 13bps and seeing potential for around 12bps if recoveries materialise.  Other fee-based businesses are showing stronger momentum. Wealth sales increased 35% year-on-year as at June 2026, while bancassurance and takaful, brokerage, investment banking and loan-related fees have continued to improve.  HLIB said these areas should partially cushion the weaker trading contribution, although elevated bond yields have made the upper end of the ROE target more difficult to achieve.  HLIB said RHB’s asset quality outlook remains manageable, with management seeing no significant corporate credit concerns at present.  Gross impaired loan formation continues to come mainly from the SME and community banking segments, but the deterioration has been gradual rather than broad-based.  Potential recoveries could emerge from the corporate, commercial and Singapore portfolios, although management is not assuming substantial write-backs.  RHB is also maintaining underwriting discipline, remaining selective in mortgages and SME lending and avoiding aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns are unattractive.  Deposit competition remains manageable, while initiatives such as RHB Pay are aimed at capturing operating balances and structurally improving current and savings account deposits and funding costs.  HLIB said capital management remains one of RHB’s more important medium-term catalysts, with the bank targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by 1Q27.  A roughly 100-basis-point uplift in the CET1 ratio, equivalent to around RM2 billion, could potentially emerge following Basel III reforms in January 2028.  Management’s priority, however, remains ensuring that normal operations and targeted growth can be adequately funded while maintaining CET1 around current levels.  Any excess capital could potentially be returned to shareholders if future growth requirements do not absorb the surplus.  The stock currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5%, while a possible normalisation in the Overnight Policy Rate from 2.75% to 3.00% in 2027 could provide another earnings lever.  HLIB maintained its RM8.00 target price, based on an implied 1.0 times CY2027 price-to-book multiple, saying current valuations already reflect most near-term positives and that stronger catalysts are needed before it adopts a more constructive stance.

title: Phoenix Distributing Expands Custom Home Builder Outreach with Addition of Dawn Lohr
body: Oct 6, 2026 Charleston-based residential fire protection company welcomes Dawn Lohr as Builder Partnerships Manager to strengthen relationships with custom home builders throughout the Lowcountry. Charleston, United States, October 6, 2026 -- Phoenix Distributing, LLC, a residential fire protection company specializing in residential fire sprinkler solutions, today announced that Dawn Lohr has joined the company as Builder Partnerships Manager. In her new role, Lohr will focus on developing and supporting relationships with custom home builders, developers and other residential construction professionals throughout the Charleston area and surrounding Lowcountry. As Phoenix Distributing continues expanding its residential fire sprinkler capabilities and builder-focused services, Lohr will serve as an important connection between the company and the residential construction community. Her responsibilities will include builder outreach, relationship development, educational initiatives and helping construction professionals better understand the planning and coordination involved in incorporating residential fire sprinkler systems into new homes. Dawn Lohr, Builder Partnerships Manager at Phoenix Distributing, works with a custom home builder on residential fire protection planning in the South Carolina Lowcountry. "Residential fire protection works best when it is considered early in the construction process and coordinated closely with the builder," said Phoenix Distributing CEO Charlie Stewart. "Dawn's ability to build relationships and communicate effectively makes her an excellent fit for what we're building at Phoenix. We want builders to view us as a long-term residential fire protection partner rather than simply another subcontractor." Lohr is based in Charleston and holds a degree in Marketing from Loyola University Maryland. She brings an entrepreneurial background and extensive experience building relationships, communicating with diverse audiences and developing community connections. In addition to her business career, Lohr is a published author and speaker. "I am excited to join Phoenix Distributing and have the opportunity to work directly with builders throughout the Lowcountry," said Lohr. "Residential fire sprinklers are an important part of protecting families and homes, and I look forward to helping builders better understand the solutions, resources and support Phoenix can provide." Phoenix Distributing works with custom home builders, developers, contractors, plumbing professionals and other industry partners to provide residential fire sprinkler expertise from project planning and design through supply, installation and inspection support. The company's approach is designed to make residential fire protection easier to coordinate within the home-building process while supporting applicable project and code requirements. The addition of Lohr comes as Phoenix increases its outreach to custom home builders throughout coastal South Carolina, including the greater Charleston area and communities extending along the Lowcountry coast. About Phoenix Distributing, LLC Phoenix Distributing, LLC specializes in residential fire protection solutions with decades of industry experience in residential fire sprinkler design, supply, installation and support. Through its specialized brands and operating companies, Phoenix provides builders and industry professionals with an integrated resource for residential fire sprinkler systems, technical expertise, education and field support. Phoenix is committed to advancing residential fire protection through professional expertise, education, innovation and strong partnerships with the building community. title: Optimistic outlook for equities in fourth quarter
body: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia’s resilient domestic economy, alongside Budget 2027, should support the local stock market in the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q26), although geopolitical uncertainty and elevated global yields could keep a lid on valuations, says MBSB Research. In a strategy report, the research house said it remained “optimistic but cautious” on Malaysian equities, favouring defensive sectors while selectively taking on growth exposure. The research house said market direction in 4Q26 would depend on whether the Strait of Hormuz begins to reopen, oil and freight costs moderate, and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) September rate hike proves to be an adjustment rather than the start of a prolonged tightening cycle. It said Malaysia’s resilient economic growth, corporate earnings and domestic liquidity should provide downside support, while Budget 2027 could bring renewed attention to domestic catalysts. However, sustained oil prices above US$100 a barrel, further Fed rate hikes and persistently elevated bond yields could continue to weigh on valuations and foreign fund flows. Despite heightened external uncertainties, MBSB Research said growth should remain well anchored, with the strong first-half (1H26) performance providing a solid base for the rest of the year, “which we expect to remain reassuring in 3Q26”. Even under more adverse scenarios, the research house said full-year growth should remain above 4%, given the strong 1H26 performance. “Into 2027, we favour sectors combining near-term catalysts with recurring demand, pricing power and resilience against prolonged external disruption,” it said. “Preference should remain with companies offering visible earnings, recurring demand, balance-sheet strength, dividend support and direct exposure to Malaysia’s domestic investment cycle.” Against this backdrop, the research house favours utilities, telecommunications, consumer staples and healthcare for their resilient earnings, while construction and technology offer exposure to growth. MBSB Research also recommended retaining exposure to plantations and energy-related stocks as protection against external uncertainty in 4Q26. Plantations could benefit from firm crude palm oil prices, biodiesel demand and ringgit weakness, while energy infrastructure and shipping should remain relevant amid normalising trade and potential supply disruptions, it said. MBSB Research expects Malaysia’s economic growth to moderate to 4.6% in 2027 from a forecast 5.1% this year, having expanded 5.7% year-on-year in 1H26. It said the moderation largely reflected normalisation from a relatively high base rather than a material weakening in underlying economic conditions. The research firm said domestic demand should remain supportive, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, positive wage growth and continued investment activity, while external trade should continue to benefit from resilient electrical and electronics (E&E) demand. Still, MBSB Research said the outlook for 2027 remained clouded by geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, including the US midterm elections, conflicts involving the United States, Iran and Israel, risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, inflation and the path of monetary policy. “A change in any one of these variables could materially alter the direction of energy prices, interest rates, global growth and financial markets, making a single-point forecast inadequate,” it noted. The research house said the next major political event to watch was the US midterm elections on Nov 3, which will determine control of the US House of Representatives and Senate. The research house said the election would not directly determine the actions of Iran, Israel or the Houthis, but could affect areas including war funding, sanctions, congressional oversight, the legal basis for military operations and the political cost of sustaining the blockade. Under its baseline scenario, where Malaysia’s economy grows 4.6% in 2027, MBSB Research expects corporate earnings to expand 6.6% and has set a preliminary FBM KLCI target of 1,850 points. The target is based on a forecast 2027 price-to-earnings ratio (PER) of 15.4 times, compared with the FBM KLCI’s current 2026 PER of 14.8 times. “Underpinned by our baseline expectations of resilient macro performance along with healthy earnings growth next year, we expect equity valuations to improve going forward,” it said. It expects the local equity market to benefit from an anticipated easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, with Brent crude oil prices expected to decline towards US$75 to US$85 per barrel. Under a more adverse scenario, MBSB Research sees GDP growth slowing to 3.2%, with earnings growth moderating to 4.5%. In this scenario, it has set a lower FBM KLCI target of 1,730 points based on a PER of 14.7 times. Separately, CIMB Research said changes to the rules governing the expanded FBM KLCI should give the 50-stock index a wider buffer against frequent changes in its constituents. The FBM KLCI is set to expand to 50 constituents from 30, with the new structure taking effect from the December 2026 semi-annual index review. FTSE Russell, which manages the index, has revised the entry and exit thresholds to reduce the frequency of stocks moving in and out of the index. Under the new rules, a stock must rank among the top 40 by full market capitalisation to qualify for inclusion, compared with the top 25 previously, while existing constituents will only be removed if they fall to 61st or below, compared with 36th previously. CIMB Research said the wider gap between the inclusion and deletion thresholds should reduce index churn. FTSE Russell has also lowered the fast- entry threshold to 1% of FBM Emas market capitalisation from 2%. Based on Aug 28 data, CIMB Research said this translates into an estimated market capitalisation threshold of RM18.1bil, compared with RM36.3bil previously. The research house said the lower threshold should allow large newly listed companies to enter the KLCI more quickly if they meet the other eligibility requirements.

title: Maybank emerges as top winner at inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) emerged as the biggest winner at the inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 that was held last Friday, sweeping home three awards including Best Financial Reporting and the flagship Best Company in IR.

Capping the hattrick win for the company was its sectoral win as Best Large-Cap company in IR for Financial Services while its president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli was named Best CEO in IR.

The awards honoured a total of 32 winners across eight main categories, celebrating public listed companies (PLCs) and investor relations professionals who have demonstrated a strong commitment to investor engagement, market communication and corporate transparency, Bursa said in a statement on Monday.

The eight categories are:

  1. Best Company in IR (overall)
  2. Best Financial Reporting
  3. Best Sustainability Communications
  4. Best IPO Company in IR
  5. Best CEO in IR
  6. Best CFO in IR
  7. Best Large-cap Company in IR by Sector (across 13 sectors)
  8. Best Mid/Small-cap Company in IR by Sector (across 13 sectors)

Other notable winners include Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA), which took home twin awards for Best Sustainability Communications and Best Large-cap Company in IR for Utilities, and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd (KL:KOPI), which was named Best IPO Company in IR. 

The other individual award — the Best CFO in IR — went to Malkit Singh Maan of Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK).

Effective investor relations is important in strengthening the quality and competitiveness of Malaysia's listed companies, said Treasury secretary general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican when delivering the keynote address at the awards celebrations.

“By communicating openly and consistently with investors, public listed companies enable better-informed investment decisions and demonstrate their commitment to transparency and accountability. As we continue enhancing the competitiveness and quality of Malaysia’s listed companies, effective investor engagement will remain an enabler of long-term value creation and sustainable market growth,” Johan said.

The inaugural awards aimed to recognise companies and professionals who are setting a high standard for transparency, engagement and market communication, said Bursa CEO Datuk Fad'l Mohamed.

"By spotlighting these practices, we hope to encourage more listed companies to strengthen their investor relations capabilities and help raise standards of investor engagement across the market," he said.

He also noted that there is considerable opportunity to strengthen IR capabilities across the market and enhance issuer-investor engagement across the market.

Based on Bursa's research, only 32% of listed companies have a dedicated internal IR function while 17% outsource the function and 51% operate without any formal IR structure.

The exchange operator and regulator said it has been building IR capabilities in the capital market through IR4U by providing practical guidance and learning opportunities for PLCs, which saw the participation of about 690 listed companies throughout 2024 and 2025.

These efforts are complemented by MY Value Up, the national capital market initiative jointly launched by the Securities Commission Malaysia and Bursa to encourage companies to strengthen fundamentals while articulating their strategies and priorities more clearly to the market.

The complete list of award winners will be featured in a special pullout in The Edge Malaysia weekly.

title: Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi
body: KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank).   Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia.

title: Maybank fully acquires Etiqa’s holding company
body: Maybank fully acquires Etiqa’s holding company KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 11): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) has bought the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary of the bank. Maybank signed the share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on Sept 8. Maybank Ageas is the holding company for Malaysian and Singaporean life and general insurance and takaful company Etiqa. “With MAHB (Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd) being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful companion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base,” said president and group CEO of Maybank Datuk Khairussaleh Ramli in a statement on Friday. This agreement comes after 25 years of partnership with Ageas. Moving forward, Maybank intends to expand Etiqa’s footprint across Southeast Asia, leveraging Maybank’s customer base. Khairussaleh added that, following this purchase, Maybank will push for faster product innovation, expand takaful propositions and enhance operational efficiency across the group. Maybank’s shares fell by 0.2% to RM10.44 per share on Friday, with a market capitalisation of RM126.3 billion. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Inside the UN tunnel
body: Guillermo R Barreto In September, like every year, the UN General Assembly commences. Heads of state take the floor to send messages to the world. These messages are broadcast on TV, transcribed, and recorded in official documents and the press. We have heard denunciations of violations of international law, calls for peace and coexistence, and also cynical remarks from leaders of genocidal entities. It is a month of speeches that surely generates revenue for the media and benefits the local economy of New York City. It is month that also entails significant expenses for the delegations of the 193 UN member nations, in addition to the numerous NGO delegations present at or around the event. The UN was founded in 1945 following the end of the Great Anti-Fascist War, referred to as World War Two, by the Eurocentric narrative. Its purposes, principles and structure are set forth in the UN Charter, signed on 26 June 1945, in San Francisco and enforced since 24 October of that same year. As stated in Article 1, its purpose is to maintain international peace and security and to promote friendly relations among nations, based on respect for the principle of equal rights and the self-determination of peoples. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Fundamental freedoms, respect for human rights, and universal peace – these are legitimate principles worth fighting for. The history of the UN, however, does not show that it has been capable of defending the principles for which it was created. Let’s look at three examples of this. In 1993 amid the war in the former Yugoslavia, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 819, which required the parties to the conflict (in this case, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina) to treat the city of Srebrenica and its surrounding areas as safe areas, free from armed attacks or any other hostile acts. At that time, Bosnian Serb forces were carrying out an operation to displace and exterminate the Muslim population of Bosnia, thousands of whom sought refuge in Srebrenica, where they expected protection from the UN through its protection force Unprofor. This protection never materialised, and the Bosnian Serb army attacked, resulting in the massacre of 8,372 people. Even today, hundreds of bodies have not been located. Rwanda is another tragic case. There, the United Nations Assistance Mission (Unamir) was established to mediate the conflict that had been brewing and that led, in 1994, to the massacre of the Tutsi population by the Hutu army and militias. The reality is that, while the Security Council debated whether to use the term ‘genocide’ to describe what was happening, Unamir’s blue helmets were restricted in their actions, their personnel reduced to 250 troops, and the slaughter continued, leaving hundreds of thousands of people unprotected; they were ultimately murdered before the eyes of a world that watched without reacting. The words of the peacekeeping force commander, Romeo Dellaire, speak volumes: “I know that the mourning for all those Rwandans who placed their faith in us and believed that the UN Peacekeeping Force was there to stop the extermination, to stop the killings, and to guide them toward peace will never end. That mission, Unamir, failed.” Another UN failure is reflected in the United Nations Stabilisation Mission in Haiti (Minustah). A blue helmet intervention was launched to “maintain peace and security and support a political process leading to elections in 2010”. The mission remained in place until 2017, when its continued presence was deemed unsustainable. The conduct of Minustah soldiers has been heavily criticised, with numerous cases of rape and abuse of women and children. The introduction of a cholera epidemic (due to negligence in the management of wastewater from the blue helmets’ camps), caused some 9,792 deaths and affected about 820,000 people between 2010 and 2019. To date, the UN has not provided any form of compensation, and there has been no restorative justice for these cases. These are just three examples. The reality is that the UN was born with fundamental flaws: - A General Assembly where all parties have a voice and a vote and pass resolutions that are merely deliberative in nature and not legally binding - A Security Council composed of five permanent members with veto power and 10 non-permanent members – five of whom are elected each year for a two-year term – who, although they can make decisions, are severely limited by the veto power of the permanent members This is a self-perpetuating structure that, day by day, seems to be turning into an empty shell, powerless to transform an increasingly cruel reality. Twenty years ago, in an iconic speech before the UN General Assembly, the then-president of Venezuela, Hugo Chávez, said: “The United Nations system that emerged after World War Two has collapsed, shattered, it does not work anymore.” In that speech, Chávez called for the re-founding of the UN and put four proposals on the table: - The expansion of the Security Council in both the permanent and non-permanent categories - The implementation of effective methods for addressing and resolving conflicts - The immediate abolition of the veto power - The strengthening of the role and powers of the secretary-general Chávez added that it was necessary to move the organisation’s headquarters to another country that, unlike the US, would respect the host country’s norms by not imposing visa restrictions on delegations that are entitled to participate in the General Assembly and in the organisation’s own meetings and activities. For this year’s 2026 Assembly, the State Department is preventing the Palestinian delegation from attending. The General Assembly reminded the US government of its commitment to respect the host country agreement and voted in favour of Palestine’s participation. President Mahmoud Abbas will, however, have to participate via videoconference. Thus, we are currently witnessing increasingly aggressive and shameless actions by the US administration. This is an administration led by a narcissist surrounded by religious fanatics for whom international law holds no value and who act consistently to weaken the UN system and the principles of multilateralism. This is an administration that relies solely on military might to impose its will and uses unilateral coercive measures (neither contemplated nor endorsed by the UN) to force countries to submit to US influence. “The devil came here yesterday. Yesterday, the Devil was here in this very place. This rostrum still smells like sulphur.” This is how Hugo Chávez began his speech before the UN General Assembly exactly 20 years ago, on 20 September, one day after the speech by US President George W Bush – a phrase that echoed through the halls of the UN and made its way around the entire world. In that speech, Chávez unequivocally denounced the US’ ambitions to dominate the world, to install a ‘world dictatorship”, and to impose a “very original” democracy “through explosions, bombings, invasions and bombs”. Without hesitation, he labelled Bush a cynic for speaking to nations with hypocrisy while expressing his desire to control everything. Today, the US imposes its will even on its allies, wields a deadly military apparatus, and has no qualms about expressing its expansionist and controlling ambitions. The UN, on the other hand, appears to be an organisation incapable of curbing those ambitions or stopping the genocide of the Palestinian people, the massacres in Sudan, or the imperialist aggressions against Venezuela, Cuba or Iran. Can we expect anything from this 81st UN General Assembly? In his speech, Chávez spoke of the need to rebuild the UN. This need remains more relevant than ever. He also left room for hope by expressing reasons to be optimistic: “Streams, alternative thoughts and movements, youths with different ideas are rising.” That is where hope lies – in the capacity of organised peoples fighting for a different future – and not, for now, in the hallways and rostrums of the UN, where the air still reeks of sulphur. – Globetrotter Guillermo R Barreto is Venezuelan and holds a PhD in science from the University of Oxford). A retired professor at Simón Bolívar University in Venezuela, he served as the country’s deputy science and technology minister, president of the National Fund for Science and Technology, and ecosocialism and water minister. He is currently a researcher at the Tricontinental Institute for Social Research and a visiting scholar at the Center for the Study of Social Transformations-Ivic. title: Mesiniaga Wins Two-year RM32.3m Contract Extension From Customs Dept
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MYGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. According to the company’s bourse filing on Tuesday, the agreement does not include an automatic renewal clause. The MyGST system is the Customs Department's legacy online system for administering goods and services tax (GST), which was Malaysia's broad-based consumption tax from April 2015 until its abolition in September 2018. Malaysia's current sales and service tax (SST) system is administered through MySST, but MyGST system remains in operation as the agency maintains it to support other tax administrative matters, fulfil statutory/legal requirements and work procedures. Mesiniaga said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the group’s earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026) and subsequent periods until completion. For the first half of FY2026, Mesiniaga’s net loss narrowed to RM0.95 million from RM2.13 million in the previous period, while revenue was up by 22.4% to RM113.2 million. The group said it saw higher revenue from projects and services deliveries. Shares of Mesiniaga were down by one sen or 0.9% to RM1.16 at market close on Tuesday, giving the group a market value of RM70.1 million. title: Banking Sector - FBM KLCI 50: Lower Bank Weight, Limited Passive Impact
body: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) will expand from 30 to 50 constituents in December, reflecting the significant growth in Bursa Malaysia's market capitalisation and the broader depth of its listed universe. While the FBM KLCI remains the country's flagship equity benchmark, its current 30 constituents represent only about 60% of the market's total capitalisation, below the approximately 70% coverage typically achieved by major global large-cap indices. The expansion aims to provide a broader representation of the Malaysian equity market while enhancing sector diversification through greater exposure to Technology, Energy and Industrials. To facilitate a smooth transition and minimise potential market disruption, the 20 additional constituents will be introduced in two stages. In the first phase, effective 21 December 2026, the new entrants will be included at 50% of their eventual index weights. The selection cut-off date will be 23 November 2026, with the final list of constituents announced on 3 December 2026. The second phase, effective 21 June 2027, will increase these constituents to their full index weights, completing the transition. Concurrently, the FBM Mid 70 Index will be streamlined to 50 constituents and rebranded as the FBM Mid Cap Index, while the overall FBM Top 100 Index universe remains unchanged at 100 stocks. The expansion is expected to create a more diversified and less concentrated benchmark. Based on market data as at 30 June 2026, the weight of the largest constituent is projected to decline from 13.2% to approximately 11.1% upon completion of Phase 2. Similarly, the combined weighting of the top five constituents is expected to fall from 50.0% to 42.1%, while the top 10 stocks will account for 57.2% of the index versus 67.9% under the current composition. The expanded FBM KLCI will also better represent non-financial sectors. Technology stocks will enter the benchmark for the first time, with an estimated 2.4% weighting upon full implementation. Industrials is expected to increase from 6.2% to 9.1%, Consumer Discretionary from 0.9% to 2.9%, Real Estate from 3.1% to 4.0%, and Energy from 1.0% to 2.0%. For the banking sector, the key implication is a structural dilution in index representation rather than a change in fundamentals. Financials' weighting is expected to decline from 42.7% currently to 39.4% in Phase 1 and 36.6% after Phase 2 is completed. In contrast, financial stocks will be more represented in the revamped FBM Mid Cap Index, with the sector's weighting projected to increase from 8.8% to 14.3%. In this report, we assess the implications of the FBM KLCI expansion for financial stocks and the broader banking sector. The reduction in Financials' index weight could result in passive selling of existing banking constituents. However, we believe the actual flow impact should remain modest given the relatively small pool of assets tracking the FBM KLCI. Based on our estimate of approximately RM3.0bn in KLCI-tracking passive assets under management (AUM), we estimate gross passive selling of around RM202mn across the six existing banking constituents, partly offset by around RM22mn of potential passive buying into Alliance Bank if it is included in the expanded benchmark. This would result in net estimated passive outflows of approximately RM180mn from the seven affected banking stocks. Importantly, the estimated RM180mn net outflow represents only around 0.06% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of approximately RM280bn across the seven affected banks. This suggests that the headline reduction in the Financials weighting is unlikely to translate into material selling pressure on banking stocks. Rather, we view the rebalancing primarily as a potential source of temporary stock-specific volatility and portfolio repositioning around the implementation dates. The relatively modest flow impact is also supported by the phased implementation. Assuming the RM3.0bn passive AUM and underlying index weights remain unchanged, approximately half of the estimated flow would occur during Phase 1 in December 2026, with the remaining adjustment taking place when the new constituents reach their full weights in June 2027. This should reduce the immediate impact of the rebalancing on banking stocks. While we estimate KLCI-tracking passive AUM at approximately RM3.0bn, the actual pool could differ depending on how much is benchmarked to the index. To assess the sensitivity of our conclusion, we estimate the potential net banking-sector outflows under different passive AUM assumptions Even under a higher RM5.0bn passive-AUM assumption, estimated net selling would amount to approximately RM300mn, equivalent to only around 0.1% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of the affected banks. As such, we believe the conclusion that the index expansion represents a relatively modest direct flow event remains intact across a reasonable range of passive-AUM assumptions. Alliance Bank has been identified as one of the 20 indicative candidates for inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI. If selected, we estimate that the bank could receive approximately RM21.8mn of incremental passive demand based on its potential 0.73% increase in index weighting and our RM3.0bn passive-AUM assumption. We believe the potential index inclusion provides an additional technical catalyst to an already supportive fundamental investment case. Alliance Bank's gross loans expanded by 9.5% YoY, significantly above the industry average of around 5%, supporting continued market-share gains. Asset quality also strengthened, with net credit cost falling to 0.3bps from 14.4bps a year ago, driven largely by recoveries from its corporate portfolio. Its 37.7% CASA ratio provides a relatively stable and low-cost funding base, which should help the bank manage ongoing deposit repricing pressures and preserve NIM. Hence, Alliance Bank offers both a fundamental and technical catalyst - stronger-than-industry loan growth and asset quality on the one hand, and potential incremental demand from KLCItracking passive funds on the other. If confirmed as an index constituent, greater benchmark visibility could also increase its relevance among institutional investors. With the estimated index-related flows relatively small, we believe earnings delivery, NIM trends, credit costs and capital returns will remain the key determinants of banking-sector valuations. The sector continues to benefit from steady loan growth, resilient non-interest income, sound asset quality, and healthy capital and liquidity buffers. We forecast sector earnings growth of 4.8% in CY26 and 5.1% in CY27, while average return on equity is expected to remain stable at approximately 10.2%-10.3%. Malaysian banks also remain a key source of dividend yield, with sector dividend yields expected to increase from an average of 4.8% in CY25 to 5.2% in CY26 and 5.4% in CY27. Against this backdrop, we view the FBM KLCI expansion primarily as a technical and portfoliopositioning event rather than a fundamental negative for the banking sector. While several largecap banks could experience modest passive selling, we believe the magnitude of these flows is insufficient to materially alter the sector's valuation outlook. Instead, share-price performance should continue to be driven predominantly by earnings growth, NIM trends, credit costs, dividend expectations and valuation. We maintain our NEUTRAL stance on the banking sector. The expansion of the FBM KLCI will structurally reduce Financials' representation from 42.7% to 36.6% upon full implementation, creating some passive selling pressure across existing large-cap banking constituents. However, based on our estimated RM3.0bn KLCI-tracking passive AUM, the resulting net outflow of approximately RM180mn appears modest relative to the banks' free-float market capitalisation. The two-phase implementation should further limit the immediate impact, with the index changes spread across December 2026 and June 2027. We therefore expect any flow-driven volatility to be temporary and stock-specific rather than a material sector-wide liquidity event. We reiterate our HOLD calls on CIMB and Hong Leong Bank, while maintaining our BUY recommendations on Alliance Bank and Affin Bank. We upgrade Public Bank, RHB Bank, AMMB, and Maybank to BUY from hold, as recent share price weakness has created a more compelling risk-reward opportunity. Our preferred exposure remains Alliance Bank, supported by its industry-leading loan growth, improving asset quality and resilient funding profile. Its potential inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI provides an additional technical catalyst. Key downside risks to our sector outlook include further NIM compression, potential deterioration in asset quality and slower-than-expected loan growth. These risks could be exacerbated by escalating geopolitical tensions, weaker economic activity and softer business sentiment, which may weigh on credit demand and earnings growth across the sector. title: Daily Brief - 24 Sep 2026
body: The local market drifted lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit-taking among selected index heavyweights, with declines led by the transportation and banking sectors. The FBM KLCI shed 7.07 points to end at 1,676.43, off an early high of 1,685.37 and low of 1,675.15, as losers narrowly beat gainers 549 to 519, on lower turnover of 3.2bn shares worth RM2.99bn. The local benchmark index is expected to remain rangebound as investors await clearer policy signals from the ongoing U.S.-China talks, while the lack of meaningful domestic catalysts is likely to keep market direction subdued. Immediate resistance for the index remains at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Meanwhile, immediate support is maintained at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). CIMB need to reinforce support above the 61.8%FR (RM7.43) to enhance recovery potential to the 27/01/26 peak (RM8.50), with next upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (RM9.17) and 138.2%FP (RM9.58) ahead, while stronger retracement support is found at the 50%FR (RM7.10). Meantime, RHB Bank is attractive to bargain for oversold rebound towards the 50- day ma (RM8.28), with a convincing breakout above the 10/08/26 high (RM8.77) to target the 123.6%FP (RM9.14). Crucial support comes from the 61.8%FR (RM7.36) and 50%FR (RM7.02). Asian markets traded mixed on Wednesday, as regional sentiment remained subdued while investors monitored ongoing geopolitical developments ahead of key U.S.-China talks. Oil prices extended their decline as traders weighed comments from President Donald Trump saying that U.S. officials had a “very good” meeting with an Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, although he also threatened to “annihilate” the country if a deal was not reached. Investors also awaited further direction from the upcoming meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with market participants watching for a possible extension of the trade truce and potential cooperation on AI between the two countries. Nevertheless, AI-linked stocks in the region extended their winning streak underpinned by renewed optimism over chip demand, amid strong consumer take up of Meta's new AI agent. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged higher 0.09% to 8,765.30, while South Korea’s Kospi gained 0.90% to 7,080.92. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.39% to 3,936.52, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index slumped 1.01% to 24,834.12. Markets in Japan were closed for a public holiday. Wall Street’s major indexes ended lower overnight as a spike in Treasury yields revived inflation concerns, while investors tracked U.S. diplomatic developments involving Iran and China. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.68% to 51,511.59. The S&P 500 slipped 0.75% to 7,706.03, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.13% to 26,936.03. The 10-year Treasury yield surged past 5.11%, reaching its highest level since 2007, as rising oil prices and stronger- than-expected U.S. business activity fueled inflation concerns. Oil prices also moved higher following Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s address to the UN, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump warned that he could “annihilate” Iran. The shift in market expectations raised the likelihood of another Federal Reserve rate hike this year, following comments from Governor Michael Barr that “further policy adjustments” would be necessary to push inflation lower. Separately, President Trump is expected to receive Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, marking Xi’s first visit to Washington, D.C., in more than a decade. The leaders are expected to discuss extending last year’s trade truce, along with AI regulation and U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan.
