title: Bursa Malaysia jatuh 20 mata diasak tekanan jualan berterusan
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup rendah pada Khamis dalam keadaan tekanan jualan yang berterusan, sejajar dengan prestasi Wall Street semalaman yang bercampur-campur dan berhati-hati. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menurun 20.81 mata atau 1.26 peratus kepada 1,630.36 daripada 1,651.17 semasa ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka rendah 1.30 mata kepada 1,649.87 bergerak antara 1,630.10 dan 1,649.87 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Pasaran secara menyeluruh negatif, dengan kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 750 berbanding 342 manakala 495 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,186 tidak diniagakan dan 12 yang lain digantung. Jumlah dagangan merosot kepada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion daripada 3.63 bilion unit bernilai RM3.62 bilion pada Rabu. Pengarah Strategi Pelaburan dan Ahli Ekonomi IPPFA Sdn Bhd, Mohd Sedek Jantan, berkata sentimen pasaran berhati-hati, didorong oleh aktiviti pembuatan domestik yang lembap dan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing. Beliau berkata, momentum sektor pembuatan yang lembap dan peralihan portfolio dalam pasaran global terus memberi tekanan kepada indeks petunjuk pasaran, dengan permintaan institusi domestik kekal sebagai pengimbang penting terhadap aliran keluar asing yang berterusan. Terdahulu, Indeks Pengurus Pembelian (PMI) Pembuatan Malaysia S&P Global yang diselaraskan mengikut musim menurun di bawah paras neutral 50.0 kepada 49.9 pada September daripada 50.2 pada Ogos, mencatatkan penurunan pertama dalam tempoh empat bulan selepas meningkat secara berterusan. Pada peringkat serantau, PMI Pembuatan ASEAN S&P Global menurun kepada 52.1 pada September daripada 52.3 pada Ogos. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank menurun empat sen kepada RM9.95, Public Bank berkurangan tiga sen kepada RM4.67 dan CIMB merosot 10 sen kepada RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional menyusut enam sen kepada RM12.90 dan IHH Healthcare menurun 13 sen kepada RM7.70. Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI meningkat setengah sen kepada 16.5 sen, VS Industry merosot satu sen kepada 27 sen dan Jaks Resources berkurangan 2.5 sen kepada 18 sen. GB Bond yang mula disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE menurun 4.5 sen kepada 20.5 sen dan HHRG naik setengah sen kepada 16.5 sen. Kaunter paling untung ialah Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak 72 sen kepada RM41.12, Ayer Holdings meningkat 20 sen kepada RM7.70, Riverview Rubber Estates naik 12 sen kepada RM3.02, Dutch Lady Malaysia Industries menambah 10 sen kepada RM30 dan Vitrox menokok sembilan sen kepada RM10. Kaunter paling rugi termasuklah Kuala Lumpur Kepong menurun 78 sen kepada RM21.42, Allianz Malaysia merosot 62 sen kepada RM21.00, United Plantations berkurangan 60 sen kepada RM30.96, Fraser & Neave dan Hong Leong Industries, masing-masing menyusut 32 sen kepada RM21.42 dan RM16.14. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid70 berkurangan 215.69 mata kepada 17,358.98, Indeks FBM Emas merosot 148.48 mata kepada 12,143.53 dan Indeks FBM Top 100 menurun 151.29 mata kepada 11,933.15. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menyusut 163.34 mata kepada 12,013.01 dan Indeks FBM ACE merosot 51.31 mata kepada 5,482.97. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk Perindustrian dan Perkhidmatan menurun 2.68 mata kepada 177.73, Indeks Tenaga berkurangan 10.69 mata kepada 454.03, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan merosot 155.58 mata kepada 19,060.91 dan Indeks Perladangan jatuh 170.10 mata kepada 9,026.57. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama menurun kepada 1.82 bilion unit bernilai RM2.42 bilion daripada 2.23 bilion unit bernilai RM3.28 bilion pada Rabu. Jumlah dagangan waran berkurangan kepada 618.78 juta unit bernilai RM72.71 juta daripada 887.74 juta unit bernilai RM138.36 juta sebelum ini. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 650.13 juta unit bernilai RM226.92 juta daripada 510.54 juta unit bernilai RM201.45 juta semalam. Kaunter barangan dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 225.90 juta saham diniagakan di Pasaran Utama, produk perindustrian dan perkhidmatan (404.80 juta), pembinaan (256.48 juta), teknologi (426.14 juta), perkhidmatan kewangan (69.01 juta), hartanah (133.11 juta), perladangan (25.25 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (12.87 juta), dana tertutup (16,100), tenaga (81.78 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (56.01 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (49.21 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (52.50 juta), utiliti (36.12 juta) dan amanah perniagaan (60,200). -BERNAMA

title: Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. Read also: Cover Story: AI may boost productivity, but what about workers’ share? title: FBM KLCI charts slight gain at midday | KLSE Screener
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's benchmark index lagged enthusiasm, weighed down by persistent fears over geopolitical risk, inflation risks and a weak sentiment for equities. At noon, the FBM KLCI was up 1.84 points to 1,632.71, with heavyweight banks helping to shore up the market. AMMB rose 11 sen to RM6.50, Hong Leong Bank jumped 26 sen to RM22.90 and Public Bank was up three sen to RM7.46. On the broader market, the sentiment remained weak with 560 decliners compared to 477 gainers. There were 2.93 billion shares traded for a value of RM1.39bil. ...

title: Maybank, Gallant Venture expand Bintan halal hub | KLSE Screener
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank and Gallant Venture are expanding their collaboration to develop the Bintan Inti Halal Hub (BIHH) in Indonesia, with the project moving into a 100-hectare development phase. The expansion follows the completion of a five-hectare pilot zone at the Bintan Industrial Estate. In a statement, Maybank said it will provide a comprehensive suite of Islamic banking and financial services to businesses operating within BIHH, including trade and working capital financing, foreign exchange and cash management solutions. Businesses will also have access to halal certification support, business matching and Maybank’s regional network. ...

title: Daily Newswatch - 23 Sep 2026
body: The FBM KLCI rallied 1.0% to 1,683.5 points on Tuesday, as strong buying in banking, semiconductor and technology stocks lifted the broader market in tandem with gains across regional markets. Technology (+2.3%), Utilities (+1.7%) and Financial Services (+1.3%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.5%), IHH Healthcare (+0.4%) and CIMB Group (+0.3%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 678 to 458, and 572 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Tuesday, supported by renewed optimism over the AI trade, easing oil prices and expectations of progress at the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI rose 0.2% to 7,017.9, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.2%) at 25,087.8, Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%) at 47,800.2 and China's Shanghai Composite (+0.1%) at 3,952.1, while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, semiconductor stocks led the regional gains as investors returned to AIlinked trades following the rally in US chipmakers and technology stocks, with strong September semiconductor exports further supporting expectations for sustained chip demand. In China, sentiment was supported by technology and AI-related stocks, while investors remained focused on the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting and the potential extension of the US-China trade truce. European stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday, extending the previous session’s gains, supported by strength in technology and consumer staples. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.2% to 6,332, while the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.3% to 643.6. AI-related stocks advanced alongside their US counterparts following positive sentiment around Meta’s Muse AI, boosting AI infrastructure and technology shares. Meanwhile, banks and insurers pared earlier gains as Eurozone sovereign yields and natural gas prices rose amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. US stocks closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq reaching a record high on renewed optimism over AI and semiconductor stocks. The Nasdaq CI gained 0.5%, while the S&P 500 was essentially flat and the Dow Jones fell 0.4%. Technology stocks led gains, with Micron Technology rising 5.0% and Sandisk nearly 7.0%, supported by optimism over AI demand. Meanwhile, financial stocks weakened, with JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo falling more than 3%, as investors remained cautious over inflation and further rate hikes. Investors also monitored Middle East developments and the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting. US: Oil Falls for 6th Session Crude oil slipped below $90 per barrel on Wednesday, extending its decline to a sixth consecutive session as signs of progress emerged in renewed US-Iran talks and efforts continued to restore operations at a key pipeline in Saudi Arabia. President Donald Trump said officials held a “very productive” meeting with Iranian envoys, adding that he is weighing whether to pursue a negotiated agreement or “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” (Trading Economics) US: Fifth District Manufacturing Unexpectedly Declines Fifth District manufacturing activity edged down in September, according to the most recent survey from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond. The composite manufacturing index dropped to −2 from 4 in August. Two of its three component indexes decreased in September: shipments to −5 from 11 and new orders to −6 from 3. Meanwhile, the employment index increased to 7 from −2. (Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond) US: Treasury Yields Edge Up to 4.97% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury wavered before settling slightly higher at 4.97% on Tuesday, as traders continued to assess developments in the Middle East, oil prices and comments from Fed officials. In his speech to the UN General Assembly, US President Trump defended his decision to join Israel in launching military action against Iran but added that he believes the US would reach a deal with Iran right after the midterm elections in November. (Trading Economics) US: Borrowing overshoots in fresh budget setback for Healey Britain borrowed more than forecast in the first five months of the fiscal year, piling fresh pressure on Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey ahead of his debut budget next month. The fiscal deficit climbed to £77.3 billion — £8.1 billion more than the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) predicted in March. In August alone, borrowing came in higher than forecast at £18.3 billion. The OBR had predicted a deficit of £14.8 billion. (Bloomberg) EU: ECB's Lane sees inflation returning to target from mid-2027 - paper An energy shock pushing up oil and gas prices is likely to last longer than the European Central Bank (ECB) had anticipated in March, with geopolitical risks now looking elevated again, ECB chief economist Philip Lane was quoted as saying on Tuesday. "As a result, we believe this second wave of energy price increases should lead to higher and more persistent inflation, before it recedes towards our target starting in mid-2027," Lane told Swiss newspaper Le Temps. (Reuters) CN: And US discuss AI, investment on second day of trade talks Chinese and US officials wrapped up their second day of talks in New York on Monday to discuss artificial intelligence, investment and trade as they sought to advance negotiations ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US this week. Talks on Monday focused on delivering on what’s been agreed by the US and Chinese lead negotiators, China’s Vice Finance Minister Liao Min said in brief remarks outside the JPMorgan Chase & Co’s headquarters in New York, where the meetings took place. (Bloomberg) SK: Consumer Sentiment Recovers in September South Korea’s Composite Consumer Sentiment Index (CCSI) rose 2.1 points to 106.6 in September 2026 from August. Consumer sentiment regarding current living standards was unchanged at 92, while sentiment about the future outlook rose one point to 98. Sentiment regarding future household income increased two points to 102, while that concerning future household spending rose one point to 110. Consumer sentiment about current domestic economic conditions climbed four points to 83, while sentiment regarding future domestic economic conditions rose one point to 90. (The Bank of Korea) MY: To continue spending on development next year despite oil price pressures - Akmal Nasrullah Malaysia will keep spending on development in 2027 even as higher oil prices add pressure to the government’s subsidy bill. While the government is committed to development, the Ministry of Finance will manage the fiscal impact, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said.told reporters after the ministry’s monthly assembly on Tuesday. (The Edge) MY: To grow 4.7% in 2026 as Southeast Asian outlook brightens - World Economic Forum Malaysia’s economy is projected to grow 4.7% in 2026, supported by technology-related exports and investment as well as robust domestic demand, according to the World Economic Forum (WEF). In its latest Chief Economists’ Outlook — September 2026, the WEF said the growth outlook for Southeast Asia remains broadly resilient, with 97% of chief economists surveyed expecting growth in the region to moderate or strengthen over the next 12 months. (The Edge) MY: Regulations on cross-border e-commerce platforms being finalised, says Teo The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is still in discussions with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Finance Ministry and the Customs Department on the regulatory framework for cross-border e-commerce platforms. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the rules governing e-commerce platforms were being finalised, and MCMC, which is under her ministry, is the body that licensed such platforms. Speaking to reporters at the launch of the Asean-China Cross Border E-Commerce Expo 2026 (CBE 2026), she said MCMC was ready to proceed once it received directions from the two ministries. (The Edge) OIB: Applies to withdraw draft circular, listing application for RM280m related party deal to make 'essential updates' Property developer Oriental Interest Bhd has applied to withdraw its draft circular and listing application filed more than a month ago for its proposed RM280 million share‑based related party acquisition that would have marked its entry into the motorcycle financing and retail business. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, the company said it had submitted a letter to the regulator to withdraw the documents filed on Aug 18 to facilitate essential updates to the documents. (The Edge) MAYBULK: To expand into industrial property business with Klang land buy Transportation and logistics group Maybulk Bhd has proposed to buy a freehold industrial property in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang for RM35.5 million cash. The property comprises 8,346 sq m of land together with a single-storey industrial building, an annexed office and a warehouse block, the group said in an exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) MMAG: Proposes RM130 mil capital reduction to pare accumulated losses Loss-making MMAG Holdings Bhd, a company which counts NexG Bhd as a substantial shareholder, has proposed a RM130 million share capital reduction to wipe out part of the company’s accumulated losses. NexG is the company’s second largest shareholder with a 9.925% stake, while Future Star Sdn Bhd is its largest shareholder with a 19.904% interest. (The Edge) L&G: Targets RM1.5b GDV for first phase of Lembah Beringin industrial park Land & General Bhd plans to launch the first phase of its Lembah Beringin industrial park in Selangor in the first quarter of next year, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM1.5 billion. The first phase of the project, which marks the property developer's expansion into the industrial segment, covers 240 acres of the group's 2,500-acre land bank in Lembah Beringin. (The Edge) GBBOND: Reports 8.22 times IPO oversubscription ahead of ACE Market debut GB Bond Holdings Bhd announced that its initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 8.22 times, ahead of its planned listing on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Oct 1. In a bursa filing on Tuesday, the industrial adhesive maker said it received 5,333 applications from the Malaysian public for 190.02 million new shares, against 20.62 million shares offered. (The Edge) CUSCAPI: Seeks RM4.55m via private placement, second TS Wong-linked firm to tap equity market this week Cuscapi Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 94.49 million new shares to raise up to RM4.55 million for working capital, making it the second company linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, better known as TS Wong, to announce a share placement this week. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday, Cuscapi said about RM2.28 million of the proceeds will be used for operating expenses, including salaries, while another RM1.37 million will go towards payments to trade creditors such as hardware suppliers. (The Edge) SUNMED: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund cashes out over RM1 bil in Sunway Healthcare shares - report Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund sold shares in Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd worth over RM1 billion on Tuesday, according to a news report. The sale of 575 million shares was priced at RM2.08 a piece, Bloomberg reported, citing a term sheet. The price tag is a discount of 9% from the hospital operator’s closing price of RM2.29 on Monday, and near the lower end of the RM2.07-RM2.10 range marketed to investors. (The Edge) TNB: Court orders Tenaga to pay Projek Lebuhraya Usahasama RM10.5 mil for Penang bridge fire The High Court here has ordered Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to pay RM10.52 million in special damages to Penang Bridge concessionaire Projek Lebuhraya Usahasama Bhd (PLUS) over a major fire incident in a cable tunnel beneath the bridge in February 2021. In a judgement delivered on Sept 16, 2026, High Court judge Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh ruled that TNB was liable in both common law negligence and breach of statutory duty under Section 33A of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 (ESA 1990), for failing to detect and repair pre-existing mechanical damage on its 132kV high-voltage cables. (The Edge) SDG: Eco World-SD Guthrie JV sells 222 acres in Negeri Sembilan for over RM1b The developer of Eco Business Park 7 in Negeri Sembilan is selling two plots of industrial land for RM1 billion to a data centre operator. The parcels measuring 222 acres combined are being sold to Tera Data Centers, according to a statement from Eco Business Park 7 Sdn Bhd, a joint venture of Eco World Development Group Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and state agency NS Corporation. There are no details about the project planned on the land. (The Edge) VITROX: Hits record high as AI-driven growth boosts outlook Shares in ViTrox Corporation Bhd hit their highest level since the company’s listing on the ACE Market in 2005 on Tuesday, driven by its strong growth prospects amid the AI infrastructure boom. ViTrox designs & manufactures vision inspection system & handler for back-end semiconductor industry. In a The Edge Malaysia weekly’s Sept 21-Sept 27 issue, its co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng said the company’s numbers will double this year, with strong growth momentum expected to continue over the next few years. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Reverses intraday gains to finish lower after touching new high; gains RM1.4b in market cap since August Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd surged to a fresh high on Tuesday, rising as much as 27 sen or 6.2% to RM4.61 during intraday trade. However, the counter then surrendered its gains as profit-taking set in, closing four sen or 0.9% lower at RM4.30. At the closing price, the refiner's market capitalisation stood at RM2.58 billion — up RM1.4 billion since August. (The Edge) YES: Inks underwriting agreement with Malacca Securities for ACE Market IPO Yes Group Management Bhd has inked an underwriting agreement with Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd for its initial public offering (IPO), in conjunction with the company’s upcoming listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia. The company operates the “Yes Travel” brand and is a meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions (MICE) specialist, principally providing customised incentive travel solutions, as well as event planning and management solutions. The IPO comprises a public issue of 91.87 million new shares and an offer for sale of 45.93 million existing shares, representing a total IPO offering of 137.80 million shares. title: 债息升冲击本地金融业 马银行9个月首跌破10令吉 | e南洋
body: （吉隆坡1日讯）美国国债收益率持续走高，银行持有债券面对更大的账面亏损压力，加上融资成本可能上升，本地银行股今日普遍走低，马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主板金融股）更跌破10令吉大关，为近9个月来首次。 马银行连续三个交易日下跌，今日收市跌4仙或0.4%，报9令吉95仙；联昌国际（CIMB，1023，主板金融股）及丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819，主板金融股）则双双下跌逾1%。 涵盖保险公司及证券行等非银行金融企业的富时大马金融指数，也跌至10个月来最低水平。 艾芬黄氏投行指出，债券收益率走高通常会对银行造成压力，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，将导致较大的账面亏损，侵蚀资本；若银行出售有关债券，则必须确认相关亏损。 与此同时，银行也可能需要提高存款利率以吸引存户，进而推高融资成本。 该行今日发布的研究报告指出，这将对银行短期非利息收入及资本充足率造成压力。 美联储上个月上调利率，为3年来首次加息，带动10年期马来西亚政府证券（MGS）收益率一度升至4.18%，随后略为回落。 随着越来越多经济学家预期，国家银行可能在11月举行今年最后一次预定货币政策会议时上调隔夜政策利率（OPR），市场对利率走势的关注进一步升温。 艾芬黄氏投行表示，债券收益率走高通常也会推高企业债券收益率，并影响银行及其他企业的融资决策，进而影响银行所赚取的费用收入。 根据该投行分析，马银行及安联银行（ABMB，2488，主板金融股）的债券组合久期最长。债券久期除了代表债券通过现金流收回成本所需的时间，也反映债券对利率变化的敏感度。 相比之下，大众银行（PBBANK，1295，主板金融股）及丰隆银行的债券组合久期最短。 在资本适足率方面，艾芬投行认为，马银行、兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066，主板金融股）及联昌国际可能面对较大的资本比率跌幅；大众银行及丰隆银行由于债券组合久期较短，所受影响则相对较小。

title: Food Waste Forms Nearly 40% of Nation’s Daily Solid Waste, Says Minister
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Nearly 40% of the total 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. He said efforts to address this waste issue require the cooperation of all parties through a "whole-of-nation approach" involving both businesses and consumers to collectively change their attitudes and practices. “This is a form of waste. Food waste is not a crime, but it is a sin. It is a grave sin when edible food is simply thrown away,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat Monday. Nga said this when replying a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and to increase recycling rates. Meanwhile, he expressed confidence that the ministry would achieve its target of exceeding a 40% recycling rate by the end of this year. Nga noted that under the "Trash to Cash" recycling programme, the total collection of recyclable materials between January and August exceeded 7.86 million kilogrammes (kg), with a sales value of over RM2.85 million. “Secondly, the zero-waste community initiative involving the establishment of 17 active zero-waste community centres during the same period has collected over 111,504kg of recyclable materials,” he said. Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition, involving 1,680 schools, successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million. “Based on calculations of the total collected from 2018 to last year, we managed to gather nearly 20 million kilogrammes of recyclable items, generating proceeds exceeding RM10.22 million,” he said. Responding to a supplementary question from Mumtaz regarding the specific controls and enforcement actions implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government concerning cable theft including penalties imposed on third parties or buyers, he said the Cabinet views this issue seriously. “We constantly collaborate and engage with the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), including examining the need to amend relevant laws to ensure harsher penalties are imposed on cable theft offenders in the country. “There have been several instances where LRT (Light Rail Transit) operations were disrupted due to cable theft by syndicates; therefore, this matter (amending laws for heavier penalties) is crucial to ensuring we continue to safeguard public safety and the well-being of the people,” he said. title: IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances
body: IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances (as at July 31, 2026) that Lee had injected into Shenton 101, the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. The final repayment sum will be determined on completion. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who turned down an earlier offer from Lee in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments following several asset acquisitions at the time. To manage potential conflicts of interest, IOI Properties had entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 acquired Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — via tender for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The vehicle secured S$376.23 million in bank borrowings to finance the acquisition, with the remainder of the purchase price, buyer's stamp duty (S$26.87 million), planning consultation fees and ongoing holding costs funded via interest-free advances from Lee. These existing bank borrowings will be consolidated into IOI Properties' accounts upon completion of the deal. No shareholder approval needed The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as its highest percentage ratio is 3.79% — below the 5% threshold under Bursa's listing rules. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on the request of Lee, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. Plans for a 35-storey mixed-use landmark The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Lee and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The deal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion. EdgeProp reported a 48-storey tower with 537 homes measuring 721 to 1,206 sq ft. The developer planned solar panels and EV charging bays. The ceremony marked construction commencement rather than completed homes. - Axis REIT had RM250 million in acquisitions under negotiation, with one or two announcements possible before year-end, Maybank Investment Bank said. The Edge reported that earlier seven-year and ten-year financing provided some protection against rising rates. Gearing was forecast at about 39% after signed acquisitions; the negotiating pipeline remained prospective Scientex signs conditional agreement for 14 Pulai parcels Packaging manufacturer and property developer Scientex Bhd proposed buying 14 freehold parcels in Mukim Pulai, Johor Bahru, for RM580.16 million. Its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd signed the conditional agreement with Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd, on Oct 6. The filing put the aggregate area at 502.5906 acres, or 21,892,847 sq ft, and the price at RM26.50 per sq ft. The land adjoins Taman Pulai Mutiara, Taman Pulai Mutiara 2, Taman Pulai Duta and Taman Pulai Duta 2. Scientex proposed a mixed-property development, but had not determined its gross development value, costs, profits or timetable. It said more than 90% of units launched in its existing Pulai developments had been sold. Completion was targeted for 2H2027, subject to block-title renewal and applicable land-transfer approvals. Funding would combine internal funds and borrowings. No independent valuation was undertaken, and shareholder approval was not required. The acquisition supported Scientex’s stated target of completing 50,000 affordable homes nationwide by 2028. Why it matters The purchase would expand Scientex’s landbank beside existing projects. Development value and delivery dates remained undetermined, and completion depended on the agreement’s conditions. Sunway Ipoh Mall reports leasing commitments ahead of 2027 opening Shopping mall owner and operator Sunway Malls said Sunway Ipoh Mall was 80% leased ahead of its scheduled 4Q2027 opening. Its Oct 6 statement described a RM1 billion development with 1.2 million sq ft of net lettable area across four retail floors and 400 shops. It unveiled 25 brands and concepts, including seven anchors and nine brands making their Perak debut. The mall forms part of the 1,350-acre Sunway City Ipoh township. Planned facilities include an ice rink, a 36-lane bowling centre, an exhibition centre and a ten-hall cinema. Sunway said portfolio occupancy was 98%, against a national average of 79%, and first-half sales grew 5%, compared with industry growth of 3.1%. Both comparisons were supplied by the group. At the same tenant-unveiling event, group managing director HC Chan sought Budget 2027 relief on mall electricity costs and SST. He proposed extending protection from fuel-adjustment charges to malls and considering an SST reduction to 3%. These remained industry requests, with no government approval announced. Why it matters Leasing commitments established part of the tenant base before opening. The mall's operating-cost proposals remained separate from any measures the government might adopt in Budget 2027. Bomba says designated premises must appoint fire-safety personnel from April 2027 Owners of 9,451 designated buildings will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers and Fire Safety Officers from April 1, 2027, Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said, according to Bernama on Oct 6. He said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, concerning the establishment of a Fire Safety Organisation at designated premises. He said owners would receive preparation periods of six to 18 months before full enforcement, depending on existing Fire Certificate expiry dates and inspection schedules. Nor Hisham said annual inspection reports prepared by managers would be assessed for certificate renewal, reducing the need for the department to inspect every building physically each year. The department expected appointments of 6,000 managers and 18,000 officers nationwide for industry needs from 2026 to 2030. It had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase providers and instructors. The requirement concerned designated premises subject to Fire Certificate obligations, rather than every property. Why it matters Affected building owners would need qualified personnel and an internal fire-safety organisation. Preparation and enforcement would depend on certificate renewal and inspection schedules. Also on the radar today Kimori report puts Phase 1 bookings at 73% Developer Premierex reported 73% bookings for Phase 1 of Kimori Residences in EdgeProp’s Oct 6 article, following the Oct 3 launch in Bukit Serdang. The freehold development comprises 418 units, with prices from RM481,600 and expected completion in 4Q2029. Layouts measure approximately 857 sq ft and 1,095 sq ft. The current report describes bookings, rather than completed sales. Setia and Gentari explore EV charging at selected developments S P Setia and Gentari Green Mobility signed an MoU to explore EV charging at selected Setia developments on Tuesday (Oct 6). The Oct 5 media release covered site identification, feasibility, installation, operation and maintenance. No sites, charging-point count or value were stated. Deployment remained subject to further work. Merdeka 118 rating report details leasing and housing plans MARC affirmed AAAIS/Stable on PNB Merdeka Ventures’ sukuk programme of up to RM6 billion, backed by PNB’s guarantee. About 70% of office space was sub-leased, while mall agreements covering 81% were signed or under negotiation. Two residential buildings with RM2 billion GDV were targeted for 1H2027 launch. EPF raises Pavilion REIT holding to 13.209% EPF acquired 12.24 million Pavilion REIT units on Sept 30, lifting its holding to 519.31 million units, or 13.209%, on Tuesday (Oct 6). Its previous holding was approximately 507.07 million units. The notice was dated Oct 1 and received on Oct 5. The transaction changed ownership of existing units. IJM appoints Johan Idris as chairman Construction and property conglomerate IJM appointed former KPMG Malaysia managing partner Datuk Johan Idris as independent non-executive chairman, effective Oct 5. EdgeProp’s Oct 6 report said Datuk Lee Teck Yuen was redesignated non-independent non-executive director. The change followed Tan Sri Krishnan Tan’s Aug 27 retirement and Lee’s interim chairmanship. MKH credit unit discloses RM127.92m loan balance Property developer MKH’s moneylending subsidiary disclosed unaudited outstanding loans and advances of RM127.92 million at Sept 30, including RM119.5 million in unsecured intra-group lending. EdgeProp’s Oct 6 report cited the Oct 5 filing. Defaults of at least three months totalled RM25,485, unchanged over the financial year; the disclosed default ratio was 0.020%. Penang reports RM2.3 billion in approved MedTech investment Penang recorded RM2.3 billion in approved MedTech investments across 40 projects from 2021 to 1Q2026, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said, according to Bernama. Nearly 4,500 jobs were associated with the investments. The figures described a multi-year manufacturing pipeline, rather than new approvals issued today, and provided context for the state’s industrial economy. Land council considers tax-rate proposals and administration The National Land Council considered resubmitted Kedah and Perlis land-tax proposals, while Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim urged stronger action on encroachment. At the same meeting, Sarawak offered its eLASIS expertise, covering about 67 transaction types. The reports did not establish that revised tax rates had taken effect. Strategist calls for clearer Sarawak grid-access rules AGL Australia principal energy strategist Anselm Chang called for published grid-access pricing and clearer rules as Sarawak faced competing electricity demands from industry, exports and data centres. Borneo Post’s Oct 6 report covered his Oct 5 proposals for battery storage, rooftop solar and demand response. These were recommendations at IDECS, rather than new grid-access regulations or project approvals. Futurist proposes underwater data-centre opportunities Scientific futurist Dr Cathrine Ball proposed underwater data centres and solar infrastructure as opportunities for Sarawak, Borneo Post reported from IDECS. She cited the state’s subsea cable connections and existing floating solar infrastructure. The remarks described possible uses of established infrastructure; they did not announce a funded underwater data-centre development or construction timetable. Brokers assess housing support and infrastructure before Budget 2027 RHB expected stronger development spending to support construction awards, while household assistance could benefit property, Bloomberg reported. CIMB identified water, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment and East Malaysian projects as potential beneficiaries. RHB also highlighted proposed price adjustments for bitumen and diesel. These remained forecasts before Oct 9 tabling. Everly Lhesson holds formal opening in Kuching The 238-room Everly Lhesson Kuching, above Vivacity Megamall, was officially opened by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg on Oct 6. He called for more quality accommodation ahead of major events, including the 2027 SEA Games, saying Kuching’s existing 13,000 hotel rooms were insufficient to meet growing demand. Today's roundup Landbank expansion and reported retail leasing pointed to continued development activity, alongside residential launches and plans for further housing supply. The reports reflected different stages of progress, from conditional purchases and bookings to leasing ahead of opening, with approvals and delivery still relevant to the eventual outcome. Asset operations also featured prominently. Fire-safety arrangements will require affected owners to prepare for additional responsibilities, while electricity costs, grid access and charging infrastructure remain considerations for developers and property managers. Hospitality demand added another dimension as Sarawak prepares for major events. The infrastructure and investment reports provided context for future property demand, but targets, approved investments and proposed technologies carried different levels of certainty. Ahead of Budget 2027, household support and development spending remained areas to watch. Their effects on housing demand, construction opportunities and operating costs will depend on the measures tabled and implemented. title: Smoky Singapore Gears Up to Talk Money Ahead of F1
body: SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. title: BNM: Banks Working Towards Fraud Alert Before Transaction Is Completed
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysian banks are working towards introducing fraud alert capabilities that can flag potential risks before a transaction is completed. A pilot test involving selected banks is targeted for the first half of 2027 ahead of wider implementation, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said in his speech text for a conference on financial crime and counter terrorism financing on Tuesday. “These alerts will prompt customers to pause, think and verify before proceeding,” he said. Fraudulent transactions and scams are a major problem globally. In Malaysia, the financial sector has prevented some RM1.9 billion in attempted fraudulent transactions, surpassing the RM1.2 billion prevented during the whole of 2025, according to the central bank’s data. More than 1,600 suspicious accounts, many of which were subsequently assessed as presenting mule-related risks, were flagged to-date by Malaysia’s digital payment backbone PayNet. The planned fraud alerts may introduce “additional friction for customers,” Abdul Rasheed acknowledged. “However, these measures are necessary to strike an appropriate balance between offering convenience and protecting customers from fraud, particularly authorised scams,” he stressed. title: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: Maybank completes Proposed Acquisition of remaining interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad | Maybank
body: Kuala Lumpur – Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) has today completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) (Proposed Acquisition) after signing a share purchase agreement (SPA) with Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas) on 8 September 2026. This follows regulatory approvals from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) that were received on 1 September 2026 for the Proposed Acquisition. MAHB is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution. President and Group CEO of Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, said that this is a major milestone for Maybank as it continues to advance Etiqa’s ambition to be a national champion, expand across Southeast Asia and build a global takaful powerhouse under ROAR30. “With MAHB being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base. Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions. It will also enhance sustainable and resilient long-term value creation for Maybank with improved capital management within the MAHB group, hence facilitating more effective capital management at the Maybank group level.” “The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank’s flagship brands.” Meanwhile, MAHB is expected to remain well-positioned to capture growth opportunities in the insurance and takaful sector. This will be supported by Maybank’s extensive customer base and distribution network, and the increasing market demand for more integrated and personalised protection solutions. “We would also like to thank Ageas for their 25 years partnership with Maybank and contribution in developing the Etiqa franchise. Moving forward, the full ownership provides Maybank and MAHB with greater agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration and expand takaful propositions while enhancing capital and operational efficiency across the Group,” added Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.

title: Era of Cheap Debt Is Over as Corporates Face Tightening Credits — BIMB Securities
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 28): The era of cheap debt is over and rising global bond yields will squeeze earnings, pushing some corporates towards bank loans, BIMB Securities said. Credit conditions are tightening, hurting firms with unhedged floating rate debts, large refinancing needs and those facing upcoming maturities, the research house said. Capital-intensive and highly leveraged companies face greater earnings risk, amplified by weaker credit quality, the house noted. “In contrast, we see tech as one of the outlier sectors — where most stocks are actually net cash,” BIMB Securities said in a note. Unlike true artificial intelligence firms or data centre operators grappling with intensive capital expenditure plans, Malaysian tech stocks is a key rotation sector for the coming era of elevated rates, the house noted. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rate earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. Bond issuances hit record highs in 2025 and corporates have continued to sell more debt this year tapping into the relatively inexpensive markets. “But this is likely to change as global rates outlook shifts to higher for longer,” BIMB Securities said. The house’s view is for the yield on 10-year government bonds to hold around 3.90% till end of the year but shift towards 4.00% by end-2027. Among the top 100 firms by market capitalisation, utilities, property, telecommunications, construction, healthcare and real estate investment trusts are the most exposed sectors, BIMB Securities flagged. The house also singled out IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) for its high floating rate debt exposure. Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) were also highlighted as both companies will have to come to the market to refinance substantial debt with sizeable maturities over the next 12 months. Banking stocks, meanwhile, could benefit from the shift, especially those with strong corporate lending franchises, the research house said. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK), in particular, could benefit from the temporary migration of borrowers from the bond market to bank loans, the house said. title: 马股半天微升1.84点   科技指数涨1.69% - 财经 - 即时财经
body: 马股半天微升1.84点 科技指数涨1.69% （吉隆坡5日讯）美国非农就业数据放缓，降低联储局加息的概率，带动区域股市普遍上涨，马股周一在部分蓝筹股获得趁低吸纳下，一度攀升至1640点。 富时综指开盘涨2.55仙，至1633.42点，随后一度升至1640.46点之后回吐部分涨幅，午休上涨1.84点，至1632.71点，上周五收盘报1630.87点。  反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上扬27.99点，至12198.56点，创业板指数也起53.92点，至5583.38点。 马股主要指数起落不一，科技指数半日上涨1.69%，是表现最出色。另外，电讯媒体指数半日下挫2.12%，为表现最差。 场内有560只下跌股，超过477只上升股，另有473只平盘。全场成交量达29亿3086万零800股，总值13亿9406万零525令吉。 有16只综指股上涨、13只下跌和1只没有起落。上涨的股项包括马电讯(TM,4863,主板电讯媒体组)上涨16仙，至7令吉99仙；国际船务(MISC,3816,主板交通物流组)起9仙，收于7令吉62仙；99迷你超市(99SMART,5326,主板消费产品服务组)起7仙，收报3令吉13仙。 部分银行股走稳，丰隆银行(HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组)起26仙，收报22令吉90仙；大马银行(AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组)涨11仙，收于6令吉50仙；大众银行(PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)升高4仙，至4令吉70仙；但马来亚银行(MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)却下挫2仙，至10令吉。 杨忠礼双雄双双走低，杨忠礼电力(YTLPOWR,6742,主板公用事业组)收报5令吉59仙，下跌9仙；杨忠礼机构(YTL,4677,主板公用事业组)收于2令吉19仙，下滑5仙。 ZETRIX公司(ZETRIX,0138,主板科技组)成为今天的市场焦点，该公司遭陆路交通局（JPJ）暂停代收服务之后，周一暂停交易一个小时，复牌之后股价应声下挫。 ZETRIX公司今早发文告证实，JPJ收款服务将于今日起暂停，该公司正在讨论解决此问题。 ZETRIX公司恢复交易后先跌至8仙，下滑3.5仙或30.43%，盘中最低跌至6.5仙，下挫5仙或43.48%，午休收于8仙，半天下滑3.5仙或30.43%，成交量更是突破8亿股，达到8亿6840万2700股成交，为全场最大热门股。  热门新闻 百格视频

title: The socialist tinge running through Malay society and politics | Opinion | The Vibes
body: By Murray Hunter A CONSISTENT thread of light, humanitarian socialism, the social-democratic and developmental variety, has long run through Malay society and politics in Malaysia. It appears in traditional cultural traits, interpretations of Islamic social ethics, the policies of major Malay parties including UMNO and PAS, and the structure of the modern economy. This form of socialism today is focused on mutual help, social justice, state intervention for equity, and protection of the community, especially the Malay majority. Private ownership, markets and individual enterprise remain, but they operate within a framework of collective responsibility and guided redistribution, through both the New Economic Policy (NEP) and reserved Malay land. Several deep-rooted Malay cultural traits help explain why such ideas found fertile ground throughout Malaya’s contemporary history. Almost forgotten traditions in the traditional kampong, gotong royong was a practical expression of communal cooperation. Villagers regularly came together to build or repair houses, plant and harvest rice, clear drains and paths, maintain the surau or cemetery, and assist with weddings, funerals and other life-cycle events. The familiar proverb “berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing” captured the expectation that burdens should be shared. More broadly, Malay society has tended to favour communalism rather than strong individualism. Group harmony, collective responsibility, loyalty to kin and community, and the avoidance of open confrontation often take precedence over assertive personal autonomy or pure self-interest. This cultural orientation creates a natural affinity for policies that stress mutual support, shared welfare and the idea that the community’s well-being is more important than unchecked individual gain. This is partly explained by Malaysia’s high power-distance score on widely used cultural dimensions such as those developed by Geert Hofstede. In high power-distance societies, hierarchy is accepted as normal, and people are generally more willing to follow authority without extensive public questioning. Among many Malays, this has historically translated into relatively high deference to traditional leaders, the state, religious figures and those in positions of formal power. When government programmes are presented as serving the uplift of the Malay community, this readiness to accept direction from above has made large-scale state intervention more readily accepted than it might be in strongly individualistic, low power-distance cultures. The combination of communalism and hierarchical acceptance helped legitimise ambitious top-down social and economic programmes. Islamic teachings have reinforced the same outlook for many. Obligatory zakat functions as a structured redistribution of wealth from those with surplus to the poor, the needy, debtors and other designated categories. The duty to care for orphans, widows and the vulnerable, the prohibition of riba (usury), and the repeated Qur’anic emphasis on adl (justice) have been interpreted by some Muslim thinkers as containing important socialist elements. Early PAS leader Burhanuddin al-Helmy explicitly combined Islamist, nationalist and socialist ideas in the struggle against colonialism and inequality. Malaysian sociologist Syed Hussein Alatas, in his work Islam and Socialism, argued that Islam’s principles of anti-exploitation and social justice made it compatible with non-Marxist forms of socialism focused on fairness and community welfare rather than atheistic materialism or the abolition of private property. In formal politics, the pattern is clear. Early Malay leftist and populist groups drew on ideas of uplifting ordinary people (marhaen). Within UMNO, the decisive shift came after the 1969 racial riots under Tun Abdul Razak. Razak, who had been exposed to British Labour Party and Fabian socialist thought during his studies, spoke of a form of “nationalist socialism” suited to a developing multi-ethnic nation. The New Economic Policy (NEP) that followed introduced large-scale state intervention with two main prongs: the eradication of poverty regardless of race, and the restructuring of society so that Malays and other Bumiputera could participate more fully in the modern economy and no longer be identified primarily with subsistence agriculture. This was deliberate social engineering aimed at equity and national unity. Key institutions created or expanded in the Razak era still shape Malaysia today. FELDA (Federal Land Development Authority) organised large-scale land settlement schemes that moved hundreds of thousands of rural Malay families onto new agricultural plots, complete with housing, infrastructure, technical support and a structured pathway out of poverty. It was a classic state-led redistributive and developmental programme. MARA (Majlis Amanah Rakyat) was established to advance Bumiputera participation in education, skills training, business and entrepreneurship through scholarships, loans, commercial ventures and institutional support. Together with other agencies, these bodies embodied the belief that the state had a positive duty to correct economic imbalances and uplift the Malay community through organised collective effort. There was an assumption that those privileged leaders would always take the interests of the people into action. PAS has contributed its own version of this tinge. Although primarily an Islamist party, it has at various times emphasised welfare provision, rural development, anti-elite rhetoric and social justice framed through Islamic ethics. In the states it has governed for long periods, PAS has pursued policies with clear redistributive and protective elements that appeal to lower-income and rural Malays who value collective support and moral economy over pure market outcomes. That is partly the reason PAS has been in government there for a long period of time. Today’s economy is reflective of this history The contemporary Malaysian economy continues to reflect the Razak-era model and retains strong features of a light socialist or developmentalist system. Government-linked companies (GLCs) play a dominant role in strategic sectors. The public bureaucracy remains large and central in directing economic activity, allocating resources and implementing preferential policies. Equity ownership targets, subsidies, public education and housing programmes, and extensive state involvement in the economy persist. FELDA and MARA continue to operate alongside a wider network of agencies dedicated to Bumiputera economic advancement. Markets and private enterprise function, freehold land ownership is secure, and individual initiative is encouraged, yet they operate within a framework of heavy government guidance and redistributive goals aimed at social and ethnic equity. This is a mixed economy with a pronounced interventionist and welfare character. The Malaysian economy is not laissez-faire capitalism, nor is it Soviet-style central planning. The focus has always been practical and humanitarian, aimed at reducing poverty, correcting historical imbalances, fostering mutual support, and using the state as an instrument of community uplift. Cultural communalism, acceptance of hierarchy, Islamic ethics of justice, and the institutional legacy of Tun Razak’s era have all sustained this approach. The light socialist colouring remains one of the quieter but durable features of Malay society and politics. It can be traced from the kampong practices of gotong royong and communalism, through the cultural readiness to accept authoritative direction for the common good, the ethical teachings of Islam on justice and redistribution, the ambitious nation-building of Tun Razak’s time with institutions such as FELDA and MARA, and the continuing role of GLCs and state guidance in today’s economy. Unfortunately, many politicians today appear to have forgotten this deeper aspect of the Malay political psyche. Too often they have become focused primarily upon their own personal wellbeing, status and material advancement rather than the broader communal and redistributive responsibilities that once animated Malay political culture. When the ethic of shared burden and collective uplift is neglected in favour of private gain, the original spirit that helped shape both society and policy risks being hollowed out. Recovering an awareness of that older communal and humanitarian strand may be necessary if Malay politics is to remain connected to the values that long gave it meaning. – September 4, 2026

title: Bursa Malaysia dijangka bergerak mendatar minggu ini
body: PETALING JAYA: Bursa Malaysia dijangka bergerak secara mendatar dan tidak menentu pada minggu ini dengan aktiviti penggiliran minat pelabur mengikut sektor. Remisier Maybank Investment Bank, Jeffry Azizi Jaafar berkata, tekanan utama terhadap pasaran dijangka datang daripada pendirian Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih ketat, peningkatan hasil bon negara itu serta pengukuhan dolar AS. Katanya, sentimen pasaran masih disokong harga minyak yang tinggi dan pemulihan saham semikonduktor di Wall Street. “Fed baru menaikkan kadar faedah, manakala hasil bon AS 10 tahun telah melepasi lima peratus, menyebabkan pelabur global lebih berhati-hati terhadap aset berisiko. “Justeru itu, Indeks Komposit Kuala Lumpur (FBM KLCI) dijangka bergerak dalam julat tertentu dan bukannya mencatatkan kenaikan menyeluruh. “Minat belian berkemungkinan tertumpu kepada sektor yang mempunyai pemangkin khusus, manakala saham berharga tinggi dan sensitif terhadap kadar faedah berpotensi mengalami pengambilan untung,” katanya kepada Utusan Malaysia. Beliau berkata, pergerakan ringgit, harga minyak dan aliran dana asing akan menjadi petunjuk penting kepada pasaran. “Penutupan positif Nasdaq pada Jumaat boleh membantu sentimen terhadap saham teknologi pada awal minggu, tetapi kenaikan hasil bon mengehadkan ruang kenaikan,” katanya. Mengulas lanjut, beliau berkata, sektor perbankan berpotensi menjadi antara penentu utama arah FBM KLCI minggu ini berikutan pemberatnya yang besar dalam indeks. Katanya, antara kaunter yang boleh diberi perhatian ialah Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Group Holdings Berhad, Public Bank Berhad dan RHB Bank Berhad. “Jika bank-bank besar kekal stabil, FBM KLCI boleh bertahan walaupun prestasi keseluruhan pasaran bercampur. “Bagaimanapun, kenaikan kadar faedah AS tidak semestinya meningkatkan keuntungan bank Malaysia secara langsung kerana kadar domestik masih ditentukan oleh Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM),” katanya. Beliau berkata, dalam keadaan pasaran tidak menentu, sektor utiliti dan saham defensif turut berpotensi menerima pengaliran dana berikutan pendapatan yang lebih stabil. “Antara kaunter yang boleh diperhatikan termasuk Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Telekom Malaysia Berhad, Maxis Berhad dan YTL Power International Berhad. “Dalam pada itu, sektor minyak dan gas dijangka menjadi antara sektor paling aktif minggu depan berikutan harga minyak mentah Brent yang masih melebihi AS$100 (RM408.21) setong walaupun mengalami sedikit penurunan. “Keadaan ini dijangka mengekalkan minat terhadap kaunter minyak dan gas termasuk Hibiscus Petroleum Berhad, Bumi Armada Berhad, Dialog Group Berhad, Dayang Enterprise Holdings Berhad dan Velesto Energy Berhad. “Sektor ini mempunyai pemangkin paling jelas, tetapi pelabur perlu mengelak daripada mengejar harga sekiranya kaunter terus mencatatkan kenaikan mendadak pada pembukaan Isnin,” katanya. Sementara itu, Jeffry berkata, sektor teknologi dan semikonduktor berpotensi mencatatkan pemulihan secara terpilih selepas Nasdaq ditutup lebih tinggi pada Jumaat, dibantu saham semikonduktor. “Pelancaran global produk baharu Apple turut berpotensi mengekalkan perhatian terhadap rantaian bekalan elektronik. “Antara kaunter yang boleh diberi perhatian termasuk Inari Amertron Berhad, Malaysian Pacific Industries Berhad, Unisem (M) Berhad, Frontken Corporation Berhad dan ViTrox Corporation Berhad. “Bagaimanapun, sektor teknologi masih sensitif terhadap hasil bon AS. Oleh itu, kenaikan mungkin bersifat terpilih dan bukan semua saham teknologi akan meningkat secara serentak,” katanya. – UTUSAN

title: Maybank Upgrades HEGROUP to Buy After RM124m Johor Data-Centre Contract Win
body: Maybank Investment Bank analyst Thong Kei Jun upgraded HE Group to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised his target price to RM1.35 from RM0.96, implying 25% upside. The upgrade followed a RM124 million electrical subcontract for a Johor data centre, lifting HE Group’s 2026 year-to-date contract wins to RM416.6 million—already above Maybank’s initial RM350 million full-year assumption. Its outstanding order book now stands at RM441 million. Thong Kei Jun does not yet have a one-year expert rating on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023, due to insufficient qualifying one-year performance data. Over the three months following his calls, the stocks he covered recorded an average return of 24% and a 55% success rate. Thong expects further data-centre work to support growth, with such projects accounting for about 80% of HE Group’s RM1 billion tender pipeline. He also anticipates a pickup in semiconductor tenders in the first half of 2027. Reflecting the stronger contract momentum, he raised his 2026–2028 core-profit forecasts by 3%–48% and now projects RM19.1 million, RM33.1 million and RM37.3 million, respectively. As of 9:40 a.m. on September 25, HE Group's share price rose 3.7% to RM1.12. Disclaimer: All content is AI-aggregated from public sources for informational and educational purposes only.
