title: 马股随隔夜美股反弹，但投资者仍保持谨慎，综指仅微幅收高
body: 马股周五随隔夜美股反弹，由于市场对美债收益率和油价的担忧挥之不去，投资者仍保持谨慎并采取选择性投资策略，综合指数收盘仅微幅走高。 截至下午闭市，综合指数涨0.51点或0.03%，至1,630.87点。 市场整体表现平衡，全场上涨股592只，下跌股554只，562只平盘，另1041只股无交易。全天成交量42.59亿股，总成交额27.11亿令吉。 综指成分股涨跌互见，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）涨10仙至7.80令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）、PPB集团（PPB，4065，主板消费股）和国油石化（PCHEM，5183，主板工业股）各涨8仙，分别收在19.20令吉、9.15令吉和4.21令吉。 下跌股，雀巢（NESTLE，4707，主板消费股）跌48仙至89.52令吉，吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌42仙至21.00令吉，马国际船务（MISC，3816，主板交通与物流股）跌15仙至7.53令吉，国油气体（PETGAS，6033，主板公用事业股）跌12仙至17.20令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）涨7仙至10.02令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌1仙4.66令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌4仙至7.65令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌4仙至7.43令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌20仙至22.64令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）持平于6.30令吉。 热门股方面，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）跌5仙至11.5仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）持平于18仙，JCY国际（JCY，5161，主板科技股）涨10.5仙至66仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）涨2仙至29仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨2仙至51.5仙。 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨1.28令吉至42.40令吉，UWC公司（UWC，5292，主板科技股）涨47仙至7.57令吉；ENRA集团（ENRA，8613，主板产业股）跌25.5仙至72.5仙，安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌20仙至20.80令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.58% 至 5,634.83 点，香港恒生指数跌 2.60% 至 23,972.29 点，日本日经指255数跌 0.94% 至 68,309.46 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 0.46% 至 7,003.74 点。中国股市适逢国庆长假期休市。 The post 马股随隔夜美股反弹，但投资者仍保持谨慎，综指仅微幅收高 appeared first on 股票消息.

title: Maybank IB upgrades SD Guthrie to ‘buy’ post sell-off, cites market overreaction to PNB's exchangeable sukuk
body:
KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 15): Shares of SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) have been upgraded to "buy" from "hold" in the near term by Maybank Investment Bank after an "unwarranted" sell-off following Permodalan Nasional Bhd’s (PNB) latest exchangeable sukuk issuance. 

The research house said despite recent share price weakness, the plantation group's fundamentals remain intact. 

It added that the selldown was largely driven by market overreaction to PNB’s US$300 million (RM1.22 billion) exchangeable sukuk (ES), which has no earnings per share (EPS) impact on SD Guthrie.

SD Guthrie shares increased from RM6.14 on Sept 9, the day PNB announced the exchangeable sukuk, to RM6.34 at time of writing on Tuesday. The latest price values the group at RM43.85 billion.

"With the ES issued last week, we believe concerns over ES potential overhang are over and largely misunderstood," Maybank IB said in a note on Tuesday.

Because the sukuk was issued by PNB rather than SD Guthrie, there will be no new share issuance if investors exercise their options. 

Furthermore, there must be a significant price appreciation before conversion rights can be exercised.

Maybank IB estimates SD Guthrie's share price would need to hit at least RM8.66, which is well above current trading levels, before sukuk investors can exchange them for the stock.

"We believe the recent selldown has been unwarranted as nothing has fundamentally changed the past month except for an US$300 million exchangeable sukuk (ES) issued by PNB," Maybank IB added.

The stock upgrade comes as Maybank IB projects SD Guthrie's core net profit to be RM2.9 billion for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026), which is 5% above the broader market consensus of RM2.76 billion. 

However, long-term consensus expectations lean higher than the research house's forecasts.

According to Bloomberg data, the broader market sentiment on SD Guthrie remains positive, with 14 out of 18 research houses rating the stock as a "buy", two recommending "hold" and two "outperform" calls. 

The Bloomberg consensus 12-month target price stands at RM7.65, a potential upside of 20.9% from current trading levels.

Maybank IB said SD Guthrie's growth would be centred on new business verticals, including industrial park joint developments spanning over 20,000 acres to sustain RM500 million to RM700 million annual income, alongside its goal of developing one gigawatt in large-scale solar projects.

Maybank IB maintained its target price of RM7.10 based on 0.55 times revised net asset value (RNAV).

An interim dividend per share of 11.18 sen declared in its 1HFY2026 results will go ex-date on Oct 20.

title: RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26 | KLSE Screener
body: PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. ...

title: Stronger MyCC Powers Put Competition Compliance Higher On Governance Agenda, CIMB Report
body: Competition compliance is set to become a more important corporate governance and ESG consideration for Malaysian companies as the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) gains stronger enforcement powers, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest Malaysia strategy report, CIMB said the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026, passed by the Dewan Rakyat on July 6, significantly broadens MyCC’s enforcement toolkit. As of the report dated Sept 15, CIMB noted that the amendments had yet to be gazetted. Parliament records confirm the Bill was passed on July 6.  The research house said the changes strengthen MyCC’s powers through new settlement mechanisms, whistleblower protection and rewards, and expanded authority to compel companies to provide information during market reviews.  Companies admitting liability after receiving a proposed decision may, according to CIMB’s account of the amendments, negotiate settlements with penalties potentially reduced by up to 40%.  CIMB said MyCC’s enforcement priorities remain focused on cartels, abuse of dominance, government procurement, food supply chains and digital markets, with the commission increasingly evolving from a traditional enforcement body into a broader economic regulator.  Cartels remain the main enforcement priority, particularly in food supply chains and public procurement. MyCC has also increased scrutiny of sectors affecting household living costs and industries where bid-rigging risks are higher.  The report highlighted the chicken feed cartel case as an example of more sophisticated enforcement. MyCC imposed RM415.5 million in total penalties across five companies, its largest competition penalty to date, after finding coordinated price increases between January 2020 and June 2022. The Competition Appeal Tribunal upheld the RM415.5 million decision in February 2026.  Digital markets are also emerging as a major regulatory frontier. MyCC’s review covers mobile operating and payment systems, e-commerce marketplaces, digital advertising, online travel agencies and data privacy, reflecting growing scrutiny of platforms that act as “gatekeepers” between businesses and consumers. MyCC’s official digital economy review identifies the same five areas and 34 competition, market and regulatory issues.  CIMB said competition compliance should increasingly be treated alongside anti-corruption policies, whistleblower mechanisms, board oversight and corporate ethics under the governance pillar of ESG.  It expects Malaysian companies, particularly those operating in concentrated industries, government procurement or sectors with extensive interaction among competitors, to increase investment in board oversight, employee training and formal competition compliance programmes.  While stronger enforcement could increase compliance costs and regulatory scrutiny in the near term, CIMB believes the longer-term impact should be positive for Malaysia’s capital markets by improving market integrity, corporate governance and investor confidence.  The research house does not expect competition enforcement to materially alter sector investment cases in the near term, but said governance standards are likely to become a more important differentiator as Malaysia’s competition regime matures.

title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower Amid US Yield Increase and Regional Tensions
body: Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia began the trading day on a lower note, reflecting Wall Street's mixed performance as higher US Treasury yields and ongoing tensions in West Asia affected investor sentiment. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 3.74 points, or 0.22 percent, to 1,647.43 at 9.10 am on Thursday, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. The broader market saw 200 decliners outpacing 142 gainers, with 307 counters unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. The turnover was 246.59 million shares, valued at RM118.14 million. Thong Pak Leng, Vice-President of Equity Research at Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, noted that Wall Street's mixed close was influenced by softer inflation, which eased the expectations of another US Federal Reserve rate hike, although elevated bond yields still weighed on market sentiment. Domestically, Thong indicated that the market may trade cautiously due to weak market breadth and recent foreign selling, suggesting continued investor caution. He anticipates the index to consolidate within the 1,640-1,660 range, with bargain hunting providing some support. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and IHH Healthcare remained unchanged at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. Public Bank decreased by three sen to RM4.67, CIMB fell one sen to RM7.78, and Tenaga Nasional dropped two sen to RM12.94. In more active trading, new ACE Market entrant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry remained steady at 28 sen. Astro Malaysia increased by half a sen to six sen, Jaks Resources gained one sen to 21.5 sen, and Divfex rose two sen to 11 sen. Top gainers included Keck Seng, which advanced 11 sen to RM5.14, and Petron Malaysia, which rose seven sen to RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each gained six sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively, while Jati Tinggi strengthened five sen to RM1.44. Leading the decliners, Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 18 sen to RM22.02, UWC decreased 15 sen to RM6.92, and both Insights Analytics and MISC fell nine sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55, respectively. Petronas Dagangan lost eight sen to RM19.20. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 42.26 points to 17,532.41, the FBM Emas Index declined 26.32 points to 12,265.69, and the FBM Top 100 Index shed 27.82 points to 12,056.62. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26, while the FBM ACE Index decreased by 6.31 points to 5,527.97. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 point to 180.31, the Energy Index gained 1.41 points to 847.11, the Financial Services Index fell 27.47 points to 19,189.02, and the Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33.

title: PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: Bomba’s Fire Safety Manager Mandate for 9,451 Buildings Puts Compliance Demand in Focus for Unique Fire
body: Malaysia’s move to make building owners directly accountable for fire safety is set to widen the compliance market for fire protection suppliers, placing Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) among the companies positioned to benefit. From 1 April 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM) and a Fire Safety Officer (FSO), and to establish a Fire Safety Organisation at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement is in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025. Nor Hisham said any building inspected over the next one to two years that is required to hold a Fire Certificate will have to put the new structure in place. He was speaking after launching the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur on 6 October 2026, where the first cohort of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs received their certificates. A key change lies in how Fire Certificates will be renewed. Going forward, JBPM will assess annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs for certificate renewal, instead of physically inspecting every building each year. JBPM currently has 13 registered training providers and has issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. Compliance shifts to building owners The framework transfers day-to-day fire safety responsibility from the authorities to building owners and their certified in-house personnel. Under the programme, FSMs undergo a five-day course covering building inspections, evacuation planning, reporting and maintenance, while FSOs complete a three-day technical course. With a certified FSM accountable for an annual report that underpins Fire Certificate renewal, building owners are expected to place greater emphasis on keeping fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, sprinkler systems, detection and alarm devices and suppression systems in working order. This points to steadier demand for equipment replacement, servicing and refilling across the 9,451 designated premises, which include high-occupancy and high-risk buildings. Unique Fire, established in 1997 and headquartered in Shah Alam, Selangor, assembles, manufactures and distributes active fire protection systems, equipment and accessories for the built environment. Its range spans hand portable fire extinguishers, fire hose reels, hydrant and sprinkler systems, wet and dry riser systems, fire detection and alarm devices, and fire suppression systems including wet chemical and carbon dioxide systems. The Group markets products under its own Unique, Unique227, Yama and Commander brands alongside third-party brands such as Kidde, and also provides fire protection equipment servicing and dry chemical fire extinguisher refilling machines. The Group has already identified the amended Act as a demand driver. For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Unique Fire’s revenue rose 6.2% to RM114.7 million, supported by stronger assembly and distribution sales, particularly of fire suppression systems. Executive Director Marcus Liew said the core fire protection business continued to grow amid a supportive regulatory environment, backed by enforcement of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 and project rollouts under the 13th Malaysia Plan, and that the Group expects sustained demand driven by regulatory compliance requirements and ongoing contract awards. The Group is also extending its reach beyond Malaysia through Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, a 60:40 joint venture with Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd to manufacture and supply fire sprinklers, with Shanghai Mosafe providing technical support towards Underwriters Laboratories (UL) certification. With the FSM and FSO requirement taking effect in less than six months, the new compliance regime is set to move fire safety from a once-a-year inspection exercise to a continuous obligation for building owners, a shift that plays directly into Unique Fire’s product and service offering.

title: AAGB Rejects Bailout Talk After 64% Share Rout; Analysts Retain Bullish Calls with Over 100% Upside
body: AirAsia Group has rejected reports questioning its financial solvency, saying at a press conference chaired by co-founder and adviser Tony Fernandes that it had neither sought nor received a government bailout. It also denied that aircraft had been repossessed over unpaid leases or that the government had approached other airlines to take over its routes. Management said its fundraising efforts were primarily intended to refinance expensive debt rather than raise rescue capital. The clarification came after AirAsia Group’s share price fell 46% over one month, 61% over three months and 64% over the past year. Maybank Investment Bank analyst Yin Shao Yang maintained his “Buy” rating but cut the target price by 33% to RM1.22 in a report today, still implying 126% upside. Yin remains positive because he views AirAsia Group’s valuation as distressed. Its R M1.8 billion market capitalisation is below the approximately RM2 billion combined trough valuation of AirAsia Group and Capital A during the Covid-19 period, despite the airline currently being operational. The stock also trades at 1.9 times 2027E price-to-book value, below the 2.0-times average of global low-cost carriers. Successful refinancing could provide further support by generating approximately RM200 million in annual interest savings. Nevertheless, Yin’s “Buy” call depends heavily on jet-fuel prices moderating to US$115 per barrel in 2027E. He widened his 2026E core net-loss forecast to RM797.9 million from RM335.0 million, but expects earnings to rebound to core net profits of RM730.9 million in 2027E and RM772.1 million in 2028E. Yin estimates that every US$1-per-barrel increase in jet-fuel prices would reduce the group’s earnings by approximately RM75 million. Yin Shao Yang, currently ranked No.6 among 44 analysts covering the consumer products & services sector on StockTipRatings (based on data since 2023), holds a 65% expert rating with a 7% average return and a 65% success rate across the stocks he covered over a 1-year period following his calls. Separately, Capital A’s Move Digital has proposed a court-supervised scheme to restructure approximately RM292 million in net liabilities through a potential BigPay divestment, the sale of its Tune Protect stake and recovery of related-party receivables. Despite Capital A falling 47.2% over three months, Public Investment Bank analyst Denny Oh maintained “Outperform” with a RM0.55 target price, implying 124% upside. He expects no material impact from the exercise and believes BigPay’s eventual deconsolidation could strengthen Capital A’s balance sheet, although the scheme remains subject to creditor engagement and court approval. According to StockTipRatings, Denny Oh currently ranks No.6 among 12 analysts at Public Investment Bank, with a 41% expert rating and a 36% success rate. As of 12:06 p.m. on September 21, AirAsia Group's share price rose 1.9% to RM0.54, while Capital A rose 4.3% to RM0.245. title: Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi berikutan momentum positif di Wall Street
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi pada Selasa, seiring dengan momentum positif Wall Street semalaman, memandangkan harga minyak yang terkawal susulan pemulihan eksport minyak mentah dari Asia Barat, mengimbangi trend penjualan berterusan dalam pasaran bon Perbendaharaan AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 7.14 mata atau 0.44 peratus kepada 1,638.89 berbanding paras 1,631.75 ketika ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks utama itu dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 272 berbanding 202, sebanyak 364 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,944 tidak diniagakan dan 13 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 440.19 juta saham bernilai RM164.76 juta. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd memaklumkan bahawa prestasi positif Wall Street semalaman menyaksikan Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 dan Nasdaq Composite masing-masing meningkat sebanyak 0.2 peratus, 0.7 peratus dan 1.1 peratus, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent dan hasil Perbendaharaan 10 tahun masing-masing mencecah AS$100.3 setong dan 5.3 peratus. “Di peringkat tempatan, kami menjangkakan pelabur akan terus bersikap selektif menjelang pengumuman Belanjawan 2027, dengan tumpuan diberikan kepada sektor-sektor yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. “Syarikat-syarikat dalam sektor mekanikal dan elektrikal mungkin terus menyaksikan minat belian, disokong oleh penekanan kerajaan terhadap infrastruktur kecerdasan buatan (AI) serta projek tulang belakang Grid Nasional 500-kilovolt Tenaga Nasional Bhd, yang memberi kelebihan kepada syarikat seperti MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd dan Powerwell Holdings Bhd,” menurut firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Selain itu, Malacca Securities menyatakan bahawa usaha mengurangkan air tanpa hasil (NRW) juga mungkin kekal menjadi tumpuan, berpotensi memberi manfaat kepada syarikat seperti ISF Group Bhd dan Ranhill Utilities Bhd. “Akhir sekali, 99 Speed Mart Retail mungkin menyaksikan minat belian baharu susulan jangkaan peruntukan bantuan pengguna lebih tinggi di bawah Sumbangan Asas Rahmah dan Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah,” menurut kenyataan itu. Sementara itu, Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng berkata Wall Street ditutup lebih kukuh, dengan Nasdaq mencatatkan paras tertinggi baharu apabila pedagang memilih untuk tidak mempedulikan cabaran pasaran semasa dan sebaliknya menumpukan perhatian kepada saham berkaitan AI bagi mengimbangi kesan kenaikan hasil bon. “Untuk hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks akan bergerak dalam julat 1,630-1,640 memandangkan pasaran saham tempatan mungkin bersedia untuk aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah,” katanya kepada Bernama. title: One of Top Plantation Analysts Turns Cautious as Indonesia’s Land Reform Clouds Sector Outlook
body: Maybank Investment Bank analyst Ong Chee Ting downgraded his three-month view on regional plantations to “Neutral” from “Positive” after Indonesia passed a new agrarian reform law on September 22. The law seeks to address unequal land ownership and agrarian disputes. Ong believes unresolved questions over future landholding limits and whether the 20% land-provision requirement or an alternative profit-sharing arrangement applies to existing concessions could weigh on plantation share prices. He stressed that the law does not automatically require companies to surrender productive plantation land and has left his earnings forecasts unchanged pending implementation rules. Ong considers Malaysian plantation companies with little or no Indonesian estate exposure relatively safer from this regulatory risk. Sarawak Oil Palms and Ta Ann Holdings have all their planted area in Malaysia, while TH Plantations has only 3% in Indonesia. Separately, Maybank’s preferred “Buy” list now comprises SD Guthrie, Sarawak Oil Palms and Genting Plantations, with SD Guthrie replacing Kuala Lumpur Kepong on that list. Ong remains constructive on 2027 crude-palm-oil (CPO) prices, although strong current production and weak exports may limit near-term gains. Ong Chee Ting is currently ranked No.2 among 15 analysts covering the plantation sector on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 76% expert rating, with a 17% average return and an 85% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. Public Investment Bank analyst Chong Hoe Leong takes a less cautious near-term view. He maintained the plantation sector at “Overweight”, arguing that the new law is unlikely to cause immediate earnings or asset losses while its rules remain unsettled. He expects firmer CPO prices to support second-half earnings and retains a 2026 CPO price forecast of RM4,500 per tonne. His preferred stocks are Sarawak Plantation and Ta Ann Holdings, citing their above-industry production growth, projected dividend yields of 7%–8% and lack of Indonesian plantation exposure. Chong Hoe Leong ranks No.2 among 12 Public Investment Bank analysts tracked by StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He has a 45% expert rating and a 39% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. As of 11:26 a.m. on September 28, the Bursa Malaysia Plantation Index dropped 0.4% to 9,294.3 points. title: CIMB Says Lindung 24 Can Narrow Malaysia’s Protection Gap
body: Evidently, the SOCSO’s Lindung 24 social insurance scheme is expected to significantly broaden accident protection for workers without materially disrupting the private insurance and takaful industry.  In a sector report, CIMB Securities said Lindung 24, which was implemented by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) on June 1, extends protection beyond work-related accidents to provide eligible workers with 24-hour coverage for non-employment accidents, alongside income replacement, rehabilitation and dependants’ benefits.  The research house maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s insurance sector, saying the scheme is primarily aimed at underinsured workers and complements rather than replaces private medical, life and disability coverage.  CIMB said the protection gap remains substantial. Citing Perkeso, it noted that only about 48% of Malaysians have insurance protection beyond motor insurance, while coverage among the bottom 40% income group is estimated at just 4%.  About 38,000 claims were rejected between 2015 and 2025 because employees did not meet traditional eligibility requirements for employment-related accidents. With Lindung 24, Perkeso estimates that roughly 250,000 employees a year could benefit from protection for accidents previously outside the conventional workplace definition.  Take-up has also remained high. As at Sept 9, 8.5 million workers, or 87.6% of the estimated workforce, remained enrolled after the opt-out period for local workers ended on Aug 31. Around 1.2 million workers opted out, with 52% of them earning below RM3,500 per month.  Lindung 24 covers non-work accidents occurring at home, during personal travel, recreational activities, religious activities and other off-duty situations, complementing Perkeso’s existing Employment Injury Scheme, which applies to work-related accidents.  The contribution rate is currently 0.75% of monthly salary until May 2028. It will increase to 1.0% from June 2028 and 1.25% from June 2031, with both contributions and benefits capped at a monthly wage of RM6,000.  Benefits include temporary and permanent disablement payments, medical treatment, rehabilitation, dependants’ benefits, funeral assistance and education support. CIMB noted that fully disabled contributors could receive up to 90% of covered income for life, subject to Perkeso’s assessment and applicable rules.  For insurers, CIMB sees the greatest potential overlap in standalone and employer-sponsored personal accident policies. Employers could eventually rationalise duplicated accident benefits and redirect spending towards medical coverage and other employee benefits.  However, private insurance remains relevant for higher-income workers because Lindung 24 benefits are capped at the RM6,000 salary ceiling, while private products provide broader medical, life, critical illness and income protection.  CIMB said the longer-term effect could be positive by raising awareness of underinsurance and encouraging insurers to focus on higher-value protection and health products. It maintained its Neutral sector view, while remaining more constructive on LPI Capital than Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga.

title: Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Banking, Solarvest Holdings Bhd, Gamuda Bhd, QL Resources Bhd
body: This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Banking POSITIVE BIMB SECURITIES RESEARCH (Sept 22): Global bond markets experienced higher yields amid tighter US monetary policy and higher-for-longer interest rates. On Sept 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised the federal funds rate target by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00%. The 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield stands at 4.15% as at Sept 21, and remains elevated by historical standards but is still below the peak of 4.57% recorded in October 2022. According to our economist’s assessment, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to hover around the 4.0% level in the near term before gradually moderating towards the 3.75%-3.90% range by year end. Current yield levels appear to reflect market expectations of close to two policy rate hikes in Malaysia. However, given our view that the Overnight Policy Rate will remain unchanged at 2.75% throughout 2026 and 2027, coupled with a contained domestic inflation outlook, the 10-year MGS yield is expected to ease from its current elevated level over time. Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. The impact on fair value through other comprehensive income securities is expected to result in lower FVOCI reserves due to revaluation losses in 3Q26, as the 10-year MGS yield is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Nevertheless, the effect on ROE could be favourable, as the decline in shareholders’ funds reduces the equity base used in the ROE calculation. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) (fair value: RM11.40), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) (FV: RM8.75) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) (FV:RM8.50), which have exposure to the Singapore market, are likely to see improved net interest margins as the rise in three-month Singapore overnight rate change (SORA), in tandem with Fed rate hikes, lifts asset yields and helps mitigate fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL) mark-to-market losses in 3Q26. Banks’ funding profiles remain largely anchored by longer-tenor liabilities, including Medium Term Notes with maturities of at least two to three years, which help maintain robust Net Stable Funding Ratio positions and reduce near-term refinancing pressures. As such, banks are unlikely to rush into refinancing and are more likely to adopt a wait-and-see approach when considering the rollover of maturing papers. We do not expect deposit competition to become more aggressive from here, given that 1Q26 and 2Q26 had already witnessed intense competition, with banks offering promotional fixed deposit rates of up to 3.7%-3.8% for 10- to 12-month placements. Solarvest Holdings Bhd Target price: RM4.50 BUY AMINVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 21): We believe that Solarvest Holdings Bhd (KL:SLVEST) would benefit from the government’s CRESS Acceleration Package. Under the package, a System Access Charge (SAC) of 14 sen/kWh will be introduced. We think that the lower SAC would spur the rollout of CRESS projects, as under the previous CRESS scheme, the SAC were perceived as too high. The SAC under the previous CRESS were 20 sen/kWh for projects with battery systems and 40 sen/kWh for projects without battery systems. We reckon that battery and solar systems contracts are worth about RM3.5million/mw to RM4million/mw based on recently announced projects. There is incentive for data centres to do solar under the new CRESS. This is because the tariffs under the new CRESS package would come up to about 45 to 50 sen/kWh compared with their present electricity tariffs of 50 to 60 sen/kWh. Solarvest is bidding for 11,800mw worth of projects. Out of these, about 1,200mw are expected to come from battery projects. We have raised Solarvest’s FY2028F net profit by 13.5% and FY29F net earnings by 40.4% to account for a higher EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) order book due to the new CRESS projects. Gamuda Bhd Target price: RM5.42 BUY TA SECURITIES (Sept 22): Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), via the Gamuda-BMD joint venture, has clinched the A$624 million (RM1.8 billion) Elizabeth Drive Upgrade — Mamre Road Upgrade Stage 2 Package from government agency Transport for New South Wales. Based on its 50% effective interest in the JV, Gamuda is entitled to roughly RM908 million in contract value. Given that the award also comes with cost-pass-through clauses, we believe this should limit Gamuda’s execution risk and exposure to volatile material prices. Based on the management-guided PBT margin of 5%, we estimate the project could generate approximately RM45.4 million in PBT over the contract period. Looking ahead, we expect Western Sydney’s rapid development to support sustained infrastructure spending, particularly across the road network. This should provide a healthy pipeline of replenishment opportunities for Gamuda. Gamuda’s FY2027 year-to-date new job wins have reached RM10.2 billion, lifting its unbilled construction order book to RM62.5 billion. We believe Gamuda’s near-term order book replenishment prospects remain healthy, with potential wins likely to come from data centre projects from new and repeat clients in Malaysia, renewable energy projects in Australia, particularly solar EPCCs (engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning) works, and railway infrastructure projects in Taiwan. QL Resources Bhd Target price: RM5.10 BUY HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (Sept 23): QL Resources Bhd’s (KL:QL)’s 1QFY2027 marine products manufacturing (MPM) revenue rose 18.2% year on year while PBT jumped 51.5%, with management attributing the bulk of the circa RM30 million y-o-y earnings uplift to fishmeal driven by Peru’s lower catch quota and a temporary El Niño fishing ban. Peru, which supplies roughly a fifth of the world’s fishmeal, in August called off its main anchovy season having landed only 25% of an already reduced quota. That keeps global supply tight, and fishmeal prices in July were still running about 11% above where they averaged through QL’s 1QFY27. Grade C egg prices recovered from the low RM0.20s in April to May to RM0.33 by end-June and >RM0.40 at the farm gate by August We remain constructive on QL, given that MPM is delivering into a supply shock with further runway into FY27, and did so in a seasonally soft quarter with the stronger quarters still ahead. Clean energy under BM Greentech Bhd (KL:BMGREEN] now has a working commercial proof point inside QL’s own plant while Innofood will begin contributing from 2HFY28. Integrated livestock farming and convenience store chain segments have, in our view, both passed their respective troughs, with egg prices recovering off the April low and FamilyMart's top line turning after three quarters of decline. title: MAPIM sasar RM5 juta bantu 66,000 penduduk Gaza - SAHIH
body:
MAPIM sasar RM5 juta bantu 66,000 penduduk Gaza

KUALA LUMPUR: Sekurang-kurangnya RM5 juta disasarkan untuk dikumpul Majlis Perundingan Pertubuhan Islam Malaysia (MAPIM) bagi membantu kira-kira 66,000 penduduk Gaza menghadapi musim sejuk yang semakin hampir.

Presiden MAPIM, Mohd Azmi Abdul Hamid berkata, kutipan menerusi Tabung Kemanusiaan Musim Sejuk Gaza 2026-2027 yang bermula hari ini akan berlangsung sehingga April tahun depan.

Menurutnya, bantuan akan disalurkan secara berperingkat bermula hujung Oktober ini, sebelum diteruskan pada pertengahan November serta Januari hingga April tahun depan.

“Bantuan meliputi makanan, pakaian musim sejuk, ubat-ubatan, keperluan kanak-kanak, khemah dan paling utama bekalan air bersih.

“Kita akan cuba menghantar kumpulan pertama bantuan hujung Oktober ini dan diteruskan secara berperingkat sehingga April,” katanya.

Beliau berkata demikian ketika ditemui pada Majlis Makan Malam Amal dan Pelancaran Kempen Bantuan Kemanusiaan Musim Sejuk Gaza 2026-2027, di sini, Ahad.

Mohd Azmi berkata, bantuan itu semakin mendesak berikutan musim sejuk bakal tiba dan dijangka berlangsung serentak dengan Ramadan pada awal tahun depan.

Katanya, MAPIM kini mengenal pasti rakan kerjasama di Malaysia dan Gaza bagi memastikan setiap bantuan dapat disampaikan secara telus dan berkesan.

Antara yang dipertimbangkan ialah Jawatankuasa Palang Merah Antarabangsa (ICRC), Doctors Without Borders serta beberapa organisasi kemanusiaan antarabangsa lain.

Menurutnya, MAPIM turut meneliti kaedah paling berkesan sama ada membeli barangan di Jordan atau Mesir sebelum dibawa masuk ke Gaza atau mendapatkan terus bekalan yang masih tersedia di wilayah berkenaan.

“Kalau kita gunakan kontena, ada masalah termasuk kemungkinan terpaksa menunggu lama untuk masuk sehingga menyebabkan barangan terutama makanan rosak.

“Kalau RM5 juta itu dikira berdasarkan kontena, jumlahnya tidak kurang daripada 20 kontena,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, MAPIM juga bersedia menggunakan laluan kemasukan yang dijangka tersedia pada November sekiranya ia berjaya dibuka.

Katanya, usaha itu memerlukan kerjasama kerajaan Malaysia dan Mesir terutama bagi mendapatkan kebenaran supaya bantuan dapat dibawa masuk ke Gaza.

Kempen berkenaan menyasarkan kira-kira 66,000 penerima di Khan Younis, Rafah, Deir Al-Balah, Jabalia dan Gaza City.

Orang ramai serta syarikat yang mahu menyumbang boleh menyalurkan sumbangan melalui akaun rasmi MAPIM di CIMB 8604556678.-SAHIH

title: Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Samaiden Reveals RM238 Mil Contract Value for LSS5+ Solar Project
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Renewable energy solutions provider Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. The group disclosed the contract value in a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, four days after announcing the contracts without revealing their value due to confidentiality restrictions. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). YTL Construction, which is the project's main contractor, appointed Samaiden to undertake engineering, construction and commissioning works, as well as the procurement and supply of solar components for the 99.99MW alternating-current solar photovoltaic plant. The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. Samaiden said the scope of works includes the supply and delivery of materials, design, engineering, construction, testing and completion of the solar photovoltaic facility, with work to commence upon the issuance of a notice to proceed. The group had earlier posted record annual earnings and revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), its strongest performance since listing in 2020. Net profit for FY2026 surged 93.3% to RM39.07 million from RM20.21 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 3.1% to RM364.5 million from RM353.47 million. The group's order book stood at RM435.8 million as at end-June. Samaiden shares fell seven sen or 2.19% to close at RM3.12 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM1.75 billion. Year to date, however, the counter is up 124.5%. title: Behind the remittances: The social cost of the OFW economy
body: The overseas Filipino worker phenomenon reflects a structural economic failure that began 50 years ago, when what was intended as a temporary response to unemployment and economic pressure evolved into a permanent development strategy.  To understand why the Philippines now has an entire Department of Migrant Workers (DMW), created in 2021, along with agencies and systems such as the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA), overseas employment certificates (OECs) and Philippine Overseas Labor Offices (POLOs), it is necessary to look back at how labor migration became embedded in the economy.  From a few thousand to 10 million  Before 1972, overseas employment was marginal, with fewer than 3,000 Filipinos leaving for work each year. They were mostly seafarers, U.S. Navy stewards and professionals who went to the United States after the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965.  The Philippines was still a net importer of labor, with Americans and Chinese managing factories.  In 1974, President Ferdinand Marcos Sr. issued the Labor Code of the Philippines, or Presidential Decree No. 442, and created the Overseas Employment Development Board and the National Seamen Board.  The move came amid two major pressures: the 1973 oil shock and unemployment at home.  Oil-producing countries in the Middle East suddenly had enormous revenues and needed foreign workers for large construction projects, particularly in Saudi Arabia, Libya and the United Arab Emirates.  The United States, under Henry Kissinger, encouraged labor-exporting allies to send workers to the region, helping absorb petrodollars while supporting continued oil flows.  At home, official unemployment was 7% to 8%, while underemployment was above 20%. Martial law had also coincided with the closure of small factories that could not compete after import liberalization, while unrest continued in the countryside.  Exporting surplus labor became a political and economic safety valve.  Marcos initially envisioned the manpower export program as temporary, lasting two or three years during the Middle East construction boom before workers returned home.  In 1975, the Philippines deployed 36,035 workers. By 1980, the number had reached about 200,000 a year.  By 1983, during the debt crisis, overseas employment had become part of government economic policy, with remittances providing dollars that could help service the country’s foreign debt.  After the 1986 Edsa People Power Revolution, succeeding administrations retained and expanded the system.  President Corazon Aquino institutionalized the POEA in 1987 and referred to OFWs as “Bagong Bayani.” President Fidel Ramos developed the OWWA fund and promoted Filipino workers as “world class” in 1994. The Estrada and Arroyo administrations later incorporated deployment targets into economic planning.  By 2006, annual deployments had reached 1 million.  By 2024, the Philippine Statistics Authority counted 10.1 million overseas Filipinos — 6.1 million temporary workers or OFWs and 4 million permanent immigrants — along with 1.8 million irregular migrants.  That year, overseas Filipinos remitted $38.34 billion, equivalent to 8.9% of gross domestic product directly. When the multiplier effect on consumption is included, the report estimates that remittances account for almost 20% of the economy.  Without those remittances, the report argues, the peso could have fallen to P80 to the dollar and the country could have faced a debt crisis similar to Sri Lanka’s.  What began with a few thousand workers grew into a diaspora of millions over five decades.  The costs behind the remittances  The country closely tracks the dollars OFWs send home, but the social costs are less visible.  Family disintegration  Fifty-eight percent of OFW households are headed by women left behind or by grandparents.  Studies by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies and UNICEF cited in the report show that children of OFWs have a 40% higher incidence of anxiety, low school performance and teenage pregnancy.  Long-distance parenting through video calls cannot fully replace a parent’s physical presence.  Many marriages also break down. Annulment cases in Cebu and Pampanga courts cited in the report identify having an OFW spouse as the second most common ground after infidelity.  The result has been a generation of children raised partly through mobile phones and other forms of remote communication.  Lost motherhood and fatherhood  The Philippines exports about 180,000 domestic helpers and caregivers each year to places including Hong Kong, Singapore, Saudi Arabia and Italy.  Their departure creates another question at home: Who cares for their own children and elderly relatives?  Often, that work falls to another woman from a poorer community who may also be separated from her own child.  The report describes this as a chain of care deficits and says the Philippines now has 1.2 million abandoned elderly people in rural areas.  Trafficking, abuse and death  Since 2010, the DMW has recorded about 24,000 OFWs in distress, in jail or experiencing abuse every year, according to the report.  Among the most prominent cases are Mary Jane Veloso, Flor Contemplacion, who was executed in Singapore in 1995, and Joanna Demafelis, whose body was found in a freezer in Kuwait in 2018.  Every year, 400 to 500 OFWs return home in coffins, the report says.  Contract substitution, denial of days off, rape and unpaid wages remain recurring problems, particularly for poor women deployed to countries with weak labor protections.  The Philippine government also faces limits in protecting workers while maintaining diplomatic and labor relations with host countries.  Brain drain and deskilling  The report estimates that training a nurse in publicly supported institutions such as the University of the Philippines and Philippine General Hospital costs about P1.2 million.  After training, some nurses leave to work overseas, including in the United States, where they earn far more and pay taxes to their host country.  For three decades, the Philippines exported about 19,000 nurses a year even as the domestic nurse-to-patient ratio stood at 1:45, compared with the World Health Organization standard of 1:12 cited in the report.  During the COVID-19 pandemic, the country faced a shortage of intensive care nurses while many Filipino nurses were working abroad.  Similar patterns affect teachers, engineers, seafarers and information technology workers.  Deskilling creates another problem. Teachers may become domestic workers in Dubai, while agriculturists may work as cleaners in Qatar. Over time, professional skills may deteriorate, and many workers never return to the fields for which they were trained.  A consumption-driven economy  Remittances also have broader economic effects.  Large inflows of foreign currency help keep the peso relatively strong, making exports more expensive and imports cheaper.  The report argues that this dynamic weakens domestic factories and agriculture because imported goods can become cheaper than locally produced alternatives.  Families often use remittances to buy homes, consumer goods and education rather than to build factories or other productive enterprises.  Consumption rises, but investment in productive capital does not necessarily follow.  The report says the manufacturing share of GDP fell from 38% in 1960 to 18% in 2024, describing it as the lowest in Southeast Asia.  A political cushion  Remittances can also reduce pressure on the government to create jobs at home.  When unemployment can be partly addressed through overseas deployment, governments face less urgency to reform land ownership, strengthen industry or improve domestic employment conditions, according to the report.  Remittances also help families withstand economic hardship, potentially reducing social pressure that might otherwise force more sweeping reforms.  In this sense, OFW income has served not only as a household lifeline but also as a broader political and economic cushion.  A culture of leaving  After five decades of large-scale migration, working abroad has become deeply embedded in Filipino ideas of success.  For many young people, aspirations increasingly center on careers in Canada, the Middle East or elsewhere rather than on agriculture, manufacturing or other industries at home.  The result is a culture in which leaving the country is often viewed as a primary path to upward mobility.  What if more workers had stayed?  One of the central questions raised by the OFW experience is what might have happened had millions of the country’s most ambitious, English-speaking and mobile workers remained in the Philippines.  According to the Commission on Higher Education, the country produces about 750,000 college graduates each year.  The report estimates that roughly 30% plan to leave within five years, or about 225,000 graduates annually.  It argues that retaining more of those workers could have significantly increased the country’s stock of skilled human capital.  But the effect would not have been limited to numbers.  A nurse who remains in the country may demand a better health system, open a clinic or press the government to build hospitals. An engineer may open a machine shop or contribute to local industry.  South Korea offers a comparison cited in the report.  In 1965, South Korea sent about 50,000 workers to West Germany as miners and nurses. But the government of Park Chung-hee used remittances while developing industries such as POSCO steel and Hyundai shipbuilding and encouraged workers to return with skills.  The Philippines, by contrast, continued to expand overseas deployment.  Had more Filipino workers stayed, the report argues that three major changes might have followed.  Pressure for higher wages and industrialization  A tighter labor market could have forced employers to raise wages and invest in machinery, productivity and higher-value industries.  Japan and Taiwan are cited as examples of economies where labor constraints encouraged mechanization.  The Philippines’ large supply of low-cost labor, by contrast, reduced incentives for businesses to automate.  The report argues that if labor had become scarce earlier, rice farming might have mechanized in the 1980s rather than much later.  Keeping skilled workers at home  The departure of engineers and other professionals also affected the country’s ability to develop higher-value industries.  The report cites the semiconductor sector, noting that the Philippines was a major exporter of chips in the 1990s but did not develop a significant semiconductor design industry.  Many Filipino engineers left for Singapore and Penang.  Intel operated a plant in Cavite beginning in 1995 but later closed it amid difficulties that included worker retention, according to the report.  A similar pattern affects information technology graduates, many of whom pursue opportunities in places such as Toronto rather than in domestic technology ventures.  The report argues that retaining more skilled workers could have helped the Philippines build homegrown companies comparable with Infosys or Samsung.  Losing the demographic dividend  The Philippines has a median age of 25.5, giving it a young labor force that could support a manufacturing boom.  But many young Filipinos work not in factories in Laguna or other domestic industrial centers but in warehouses in Poland, dairy farms in New Zealand and workplaces across the world.  The report argues that the country has effectively exported part of its demographic dividend.  Vietnam, which had a population comparable with the Philippines in 1990, retained more of its workers while building manufacturing industries. The report says Vietnam now produces about half of the world’s shoes and phones, while the Philippines produces virtually none.  Brain drain, therefore, has consequences beyond the loss of individual workers.  It also reduces political and economic pressure for domestic reform.  Why industrialization faltered  The report links the country’s development path to postwar economic policies shaped partly by the United States.  Two programs are central to that argument: the 1949 Dodge Plan in Japan and the 1950 Bell Mission in the Philippines.  After World War II, the United States pursued different strategies in the two countries.  In Japan and Germany, it sought strong industrial allies against communism.  Joseph Dodge, a Detroit banker, was sent to Japan in 1949 to impose fiscal austerity while supporting the rebuilding of heavy industries such as steel, shipbuilding and automobile manufacturing.  Japan was allowed to protect its market, acquire technology and export goods to the United States.  In the Philippines, the Bell Mission, led in 1950 by Daniel Bell, recommended addressing budget deficits and weaknesses in agriculture while reducing industrial protection, devaluing the peso and liberalizing imports.  The report argues that this approach later influenced International Monetary Fund and World Bank conditionalities.  It describes the two strategies as fundamentally different: state-guided industrialization in Japan and liberalization with greater reliance on agriculture and raw-material exports in the Philippines.  The report characterizes this as part of a Cold War division of labor in which Japan developed manufacturing industries while the Philippines remained focused on commodities and, eventually, labor exports.  Marcos Sr. attempted to shift this direction in 1973 through 11 major industrial projects, including steel, copper smelting, fertilizer and petrochemicals.  But after the 1983 debt crisis, some of those projects were abandoned under IMF bailout conditions.  The Aquino administration pursued further liberalization after 1986, closing or selling some projects and opening markets to imports.  The report says manufacturing’s share of GDP fell from 26% in 1980 to 22% in 1990.  It argues that the country’s economic model increasingly emphasized services, remittances and low-cost, English-speaking labor rather than domestic industrial development.  Schools produced workers for overseas markets, while investment in industries capable of employing engineers and other highly skilled workers lagged behind.  Population pressure and migration  Population growth also contributed to the expansion of overseas employment, according to the report.  In 1960, the Philippine population was about 27 million.  Based on 12 million hectares of arable land and a rice yield of 2 tons per hectare, the report estimates an ideal agricultural population of about 40 million at the time, when the country could have remained self-sufficient in rice.  Today, the population is about 115 million, with a density of 363 people per square kilometer, compared with 135 in Thailand and 99 in Malaysia.  The report attributes rapid population growth to several factors, including failed land reform, weak industrialization and the Catholic Church’s opposition to family planning before the passage of the Reproductive Health Law in 2012.  Poor rural families often had six or seven children, both as a form of economic security and as a source of farm labor, even as farm sizes declined.  Average farm holdings fell from about 3 hectares per family in 1960 to 0.8 hectare today, according to the report, leaving many families unable to depend on agriculture alone.  Population growth and overseas employment became linked.  The Philippines produces about 1.5 million new workers each year, while the economy creates about 500,000 decent jobs, according to the report.  The remaining workers must seek employment abroad, accept lower-quality jobs or remain unemployed.  The report also argues that remittances can reinforce this cycle by giving households additional resources while reducing pressure to improve agricultural productivity.  It estimates that with a population of 40 million to 50 million, Philippine GDP per capita could be about $10,000 rather than $3,700, bringing it closer to Malaysia’s level.  Breaking the cycle  Overseas employment is not inevitable. It is the result of policy choices made and sustained over decades.  Vietnam now has about 130,000 overseas workers rather than 10 million because it developed a stronger manufacturing base, according to the report.  Bangladesh, meanwhile, reduced the share of overseas-worker income in its economy from 8% to 3% of GDP after expanding its garment industry.  The report proposes five steps to reduce the Philippines’ dependence on overseas employment.  First, a portion of remittances could be directed toward productive investment rather than consumption through a mandatory 10% OFW investment fund for agricultural machinery and rural factories, supported by tax incentives.  Second, the government could encourage skilled workers to return by offering a five-year tax holiday to OFW professionals who establish businesses, similar to a program introduced in India in 1991.  Third, agriculture could be industrialized through solar irrigation, mechanization and the consolidation of small farms into cooperatives.  Fourth, the government could fully implement the Reproductive Health Law and invest in girls’ education to slow population growth.  Finally, the culture surrounding overseas work could change so that success is measured not only by the ability to leave but also by opportunities to build a life and career at home.  Without significant change, the report warns that by 2050 the Philippines could have 150 million people and 20 million OFWs while continuing to import rice and celebrate overseas workers as “Bagong Bayani.”  Mary Jane Veloso’s release after 16 years illustrates the human consequences behind those numbers.  She left the Philippines because she could not find a job in Cabanatuan that could pay for her children’s schooling, was deceived and lost 16 years of her life.  Her experience raises the broader question at the heart of the country’s labor-export system: How many more Filipinos will leave because working abroad remains one of the few available paths to economic survival? /dm

title: IOI Properties Now Agrees to Buy Shenton House From Group CEO for S$1 and Settle S$217m Advance
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances that Yeow Seng injected into Shenton 101 — the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. It will also consolidate the vehicle’s S$376.23 million borrowings into its accounts upon completion of the deal. Both figures were as of July 31, 2026. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who rejected Yeow Seng's proposal to sell Shenton 101 to IOI Properties in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments from several acquisitions at the time. Yeow Seng had proposed the sale to avoid a potential conflict of interest as he acquired the property in his personal capacity. To mitigate that, IOI Properties entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 won the tender to acquire Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as it makes up just 3.79% of IOI Properties’ total assets, below the 5% materiality threshold under listing rules that would require a shareholder vote. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on Yeow Seng's request, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. IOI Properties' net gearing, which stood at 0.70 times as at June 30, 2025, is projected to hit 1.03 times after its recent acquisitions and REIT listing, and rise further to 1.10 times following the Shenton 101 deal. The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise, which is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Yeow Seng and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The Lee family's private vehicle, Vertical Capacity Sdn Bhd, holds a controlling 65.673% stake in IOI Properties, while Yeow Seng directly holds 3.768% and Yeow Chor has 0.012%. The Employees Provident Fund is the largest institutional shareholder in IOI Properties, with a 7.496% stake. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion.
