title: Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says - Newswav
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama

title: Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil
body: Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality. Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands. Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes. “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak. He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year. Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says. “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak. To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each. BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital. Behind the quick expansion The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets. “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn. This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes. There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees. BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets. “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan. BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.” Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent. Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs. Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe. “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says. On solid operational and financial ground Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees. For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million. This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds. The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak. The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits. Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%. The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings. “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says. Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper. “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says. On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy. The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says. Zooming in on the numbers Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low. However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth. BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027. Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year. “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says. “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.” Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met. However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL:KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO. “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low. Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover. This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders. Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income. “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan. Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group. Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up. This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements. “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan. Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk. Key-figure risk Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status. “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says. Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time. Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results. Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue. Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic. “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan. BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment. title: PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang
body: KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

title: Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report
body: Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report Nelly Korda had a chance to settle her LPGA Hall of Fame future on the course this year. Victories at the Chevron Championship and U.S. Women's Open left her at 25 points, two short of induction. Given her early-season form, she was widely expected to earn those two points by the end of 2026. A single major win would have done it, but she has not won another major since June. Now, despite leading the tour in scoring average, Korda is set to miss another Hall of Fame point. This time, it has nothing to do with her performance or scores. Korda is ineligible for the Vare Trophy, the LPGA's award for lowest scoring average, due to insufficient rounds played, though she remains on track for Player of the Year. Golfweek's senior writer Beth Ann Nichols notes that the World No. 1 "currently leads the Vare Trophy race for low scoring at 69.38." However, she is not playing enough golf to win it. Had she earned the Vare Trophy, she would have received a Hall of Fame point. Paired with the Player of the Year award, which is worth one more point, that would have put her at 27. But the Vare Trophy has two key eligibility requirements. First, the golfer must play at least 60 individual-scoring rounds, or 60% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. If Nelly Korda makes the cut at The ANNIKA and plays all four rounds of the CME Group Tour Championship, she will have played 61 rounds. However, she won't meet the second eligibility criterion, which is playing at least 70 rounds, or 70% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. Counting the four rounds of the Dow Championship she played this summer, Korda finishes at 65 rounds. Thus, she falls five rounds shy of the eligibility criterion. She missed out on the Vare Trophy and the Hall of Fame point for the same reason in 2021. She could have become eligible if she had played two more events during the season. Her last event was the Solheim Cup, which Charley Hull & co. won. In total, she has made only 15 starts so far in 2026. She is now on a break that includes the ongoing Lotte Championship, which she is not playing. Golfweek reports that she will also be skipping the Asia swing, which includes the Buick LPGA Shanghai, the BMW Ladies Championship, the Maybank Championship, and the TOTO Japan Classic. This brings her total break to around two months. This isn't the first time she has missed the Asia swing. In fact, some fans have been outraged by her habit of skipping it. Korda has not played a fall Asian event since 2023. She skipped the 2024 stops after a neck injury sustained in practice. "I'm disappointed to miss these events and am especially sorry to my fans who were looking forward to seeing me play," she wrote in 2024. She also skipped last year's swing because of injury. After a top-five finish in Hawaii, Korda withdrew from the International Crown in October 2025 with an unspecified injury, and she was expected to sit out the Asia swing that followed. It came in a winless 2025 in which neck problems cost her time. Korda said after the Hawaii event that her body is "definitely worn down" by that point in the year, and she has stressed the need to be as close to 100 percent as possible before teeing it up. But despite the reduced schedule, the 28-year-old has a chance to win the remaining two points by the end of the season. She leads Haeran Ryu in the Player of the Year race by 75 points. So that is one possible point. In addition, she can win either The ANNIKA or the CME Group Tour Championship to earn the last point. Korda is a three-time winner at The ANNIKA and can do it again this year. Nelly Korda's shortened schedule has cost her another opportunity to add an LPGA Hall of Fame point, but her season is far from over. title: HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: Kuala Lumpur, 23 September 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI. Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoritinya ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar di lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif. Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami tentang pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan yang berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.” Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas. title: Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance | KLSE Screener
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively. The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. ...

body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth.  In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding.  The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL: CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL: YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026.  Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters.  DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment.  The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.  DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities.  Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets.  DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider.  In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing.

title: MOF Backs AirAsia Fundraising Drive Led by Alton, Sources Say
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Global aviation advisory firm Alton Aviation Consultancy has launched a campaign to help low-cost carrier AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB) raise as much as US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. The fundraising effort is backed by Malaysia’s Ministry of Finance (MOF), which is helping Alton attract lenders and investors as banks and other financiers become more selective in funding airlines amid tougher market conditions and surging jet fuel prices, the sources told The Edge. AirAsia has reportedly said it is seeking as much as US$1 billion primarily to support debt restructuring, refinancing, balance sheet consolidation, with the rest for operational needs. The move follows the MOF’s appointment of Alton to assess AirAsia’s funding requirements. The Edge, in its Aug 24 weekly, reported that the specialist advisory firm had been engaged to help the airline secure the proposed US$1 billion financing from international debt markets. The MOF has mandated Alton to seek potential sources of funding and has provided an undertaking or some form of guarantee that could help Alton secure borrowings of significant size, the sources said. Alton would also be entitled to a success fee if it secures the financing, with the fee calculated as a percentage of the amount raised, the sources said. The Edge has contacted Alton for comment and is still awaiting a response. "If true, the government’s involvement reflects AirAsia’s importance to Malaysia’s economy, particularly its role in domestic and regional air connectivity," Shukor Yusof, founder and analyst at aviation consultancy Endau Analytics. “They realise that they have a fiduciary duty to make sure that nothing bad happens to AirAsia because it would have a bigger impact on the domestic economy,” he added. A government-backed structure could also help AirAsia reach a wider pool of investors. Most bond issues require a credit rating to attract institutional investors and determine borrowing costs, Shukor noted. If AirAsia’s debt were able to benefit from Malaysia’s sovereign credit rating of A- from S&P Global Ratings, it could appeal to a wider pool of international institutional investors, he said. AirAsia’s funding needs have become more pressing as higher fuel costs and foreign exchange (forex) losses weigh on its finances. The airline, which employs about 17,000 people across its regional network, reported a net loss of RM527.16 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, widening from RM154.88 million in the previous quarter. Revenue fell 14.5% to RM5.09 billion. AirAsia’s average fuel price surged 66% to US$183 per barrel in 2QFY2026 from the previous quarter, while net forex losses widened to RM331 million as major currencies weakened against the US dollar. Global average jet fuel price remained elevated at US$185.43 per barrel in the week ended Sept 25, more than double the level a year earlier, according to the S&P Global Platts Jet Fuel Price Monitor. AirAsia has been particularly exposed to the surge because it entered the year without fuel hedges, leaving it to absorb the full impact of higher prices. As at June 30, 2026, AirAsia was in a net debt position of RM2.27 billion. Cash stood at RM953.67 million, while total borrowings were RM3.13 billion, including RM803.2 million due within 12 months. Lease liabilities stood at RM13.3 billion, including deferred aircraft leases. AirAsia shares closed down 1.5 sen or 2.86% to 51 sen on Thursday, giving the airline a market capitalisation of RM1.7 billion. The stock has fallen 70% so far this year. title: Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation may remain benign despite firmer monthly price increases and rising food and electricity costs, according to CIMB Securities.   The research house said headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 1.8 per cent in July, while core inflation eased to 1.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent, largely due to favourable base effects in information and communication.   However, both headline and core prices rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM), compared with no change in July, indicating firmer sequential price momentum.

title: AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan 2026
body: KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. "Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang," katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. -- BERNAMA

title: Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher as Risk Appetite Improves - MCI Group
body: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Bursa Malaysia closed slightly higher today, in line with upbeat regional markets, as improved risk appetite was supported by softer US labour data, that reduced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening and eased pressure on bond yields. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.88 of-a-point to 1,631.75 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87. The benchmark index, which opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42, moved between 1,630.95 and 1,640.46 throughout the trading session. However, on the broader market, decliners surpassed gainers 599 to 564, while 523 counters were unchanged, 1,087 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover improved to 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion, compared with 4.23 billion units worth RM2.70 billion last Friday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said technology shares were among the main beneficiaries. On Wall Street overnight, the S&P 500 gained 0.73 per cent to 7,722.72 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 per cent to 27,190.86. For the local bourse, we remain slightly positive in the near term as the FBM KLCI remains in an oversold position following last week’s sharp correction, which should continue to attract bargain hunting, particularly in selected blue chips. “Domestic liquidity also remains supportive, with local institutions recorded RM352.4 million of net buying last week, although persistent foreign selling remains a headwind,” he told Bernama. Hence, Thong expects the benchmark index to stage a gradual recovery but remain volatile, with the FBM KLCI likely to trade within the 1,620-1,650 range this week. Among the heavyweights, Public Bank rose five sen to RM4.71, CIMB perked up eight sen to RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional climbed four sen to RM13.00, Maybank eased two sen to RM10.00, and IHH Healthcare slipped four sen to RM7.76. In active trade, V.S Industry rose three sen to 32 sen, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources inched down one sen to 17 sen, Excel Force MSC slid four sen to 17 sen, while NationGate was flat at RM1.83. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries increased RM1.00 to RM43.40, UMS Integration jumped 37 sen to RM9.40, Kelington garnered 49 sen to RM9.12, Nestle advanced 48 sen to RM90.00, and Samaiden surged 35 sen to RM3.19. Top losers were led by Batu Kawan, which decined RM1.48 to RM18.98; United Plantations fell 32 sen to RM31.06; Hengyuan Refining Company trimmed 18 sen to RM3.46, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong and YTL Power International shaved off 14 sen each to RM20.86 and RM5.54, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 61.56 points to 17,543.49, the FBM Emas Index added 19.78 points to 12,190.35, the FBM Top 100 Index went up 15.70 points to 11,973.38, the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 8.69 points to 12,069.01, and the FBM ACE Index leapt 77.15 points to 5,606.61. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.45 of a point to 178.97, the Financial Services Index garnered 99.63 points to 19,140.14, while the Energy Index shaved off 3.09 points to 829.94, and the Plantation Index tumbled 125.52 points to 8,931.03. The Main Market volume expanded to 3.13 billion units worth RM2.41 billion from 2.67 billion units worth RM2.34 billion last Friday. Warrants turnover rose to 1.04 billion units worth RM208.20 million from 973.40 million units worth RM160.21 million previously. The ACE Market volume climbed to 611.02 million units valued at RM267.66 million from 593.05 million units valued at RM205.21 million on Friday. title: CIMB Considers Selling Philippine Business — Bloomberg
body: (Oct 6): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people, asking not to be identified because the process is private. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million), the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and CIMB may still decide not to sell, they said. A representative for CIMB didn’t respond to requests for comment. CIMB entered the Philippines in December 2018, and by September 2025 had 10 million customers, according to its website. CIMB also has a presence in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, as well as some operations in China, Hong Kong and the UK. The group said in August that its overall net income was RM1.94 billion in the second quarter, and that it’s continuing to “reallocate capital away from underperforming businesses”. CIMB announced in May that it was selling its automotive financing portfolio in Thailand. CIMB’s shares hit a 15-year high in January but have fallen 14% since, giving it a market value of about US$20.4 billion. title: World Bank Urges Malaysia to Adjust SME Tax Structure in Budget 2027
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysia could simplify the income tax structure for smaller businesses by consolidating its current multiple rate structure into a consolidated single corporate tax rate, the World Bank said. The government could also consider phasing out the preferential treatment once firms grow beyond the threshold of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), Apurva Sanghi, lead economist for Malaysia at the World Bank, said during a briefing on Tuesday. “Changing the incentive structure that otherwise incentivises firms from graduating from SME status can help,” he said, suggesting that the government make the tax system more supportive for investment. In Malaysia, an SME in manufacturing is defined as having sales turnover not exceeding RM50 million or no more than 200 full-time employees. For services and other sectors, it's sales turnover must be not exceeding RM20 million or no more than 75 employees. The World Bank has provided its input to the Ministry of Finance on the drafting of the budget, like many other organisations. The multilateral institution would like to see tax measures in the upcoming Budget 2027 to address Malaysia’s low tax revenue as a share of the size of its economy, Apurva said. While 2027 is an election year, there are still ways to increase tax revenue without increasing tax rates, he noted. Apurva suggested lowering the current high thresholds at which higher marginal personal income tax applies, or placing clearer limits on personal income tax relief and deductions, particularly at the upper end of the income distribution. “Without going into details, I think it's a pretty reasonably well-known fact” that the T20, or the top 20% of the income earners, “capture the bulk of benefits of reliefs that are given by the government,” he added. title: Bursa Rebounds As Investors Turn To Budget 2027 Plays
body: The FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade on Friday, gaining 5.37 points or 0.33% to 1,635.73 at 9.27am as investors tracked Wall Street’s overnight recovery and looked for opportunities ahead of Budget 2027, The Star reported.  The local market remained cautious, however, with elevated US bond yields and oil prices continuing to weigh on sentiment.  Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd rose 58 sen to RM41.70, while IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 20 sen to RM7.90 and UWC added 17 sen to RM7.27.  Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd advanced 19 sen to RM3.83 after appointing Erkki Tapio Ranta as its chief executive officer effective Oct 1.  On the losing side, MISC Bhd fell 14 sen to RM7.54, Hong Leong Industries Bhd shed 12 sen to RM16.02, while RHB Bank Bhd and AMMB Holdings Bhd eased five sen and four sen to RM7.42 and RM6.35 respectively.  Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.04% to 50,926.74, while the S&P 500 gained 0.20% to 7,666.48 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.04% as the global bond selloff eased.  Berjaya Research expects the FBM KLCI to remain cautious as investors monitor US bond yields and oil prices.  The research house said softer US unemployment data due later could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy and provide some relief to equities.  “With the key index slipping into oversold territory, potential mild bargain hunting may resurface amid the easing US 10-year Treasury yield as well as the pullback in oil prices,” it said.  Berjaya Research placed immediate resistance at 1,657 to 1,663 points, with support at 1,625 followed by 1,620.  Meanwhile, Malacca Securities expects sentiment to improve alongside Wall Street but said investors would remain selective, particularly towards potential beneficiaries of Budget 2027, which is due to be tabled next Friday.  It highlighted ViTrox Corp Bhd on stronger demand for high-precision inspection solutions linked to AI infrastructure and advanced packaging, while QES Group Bhd could benefit from its expansion into China’s X-ray semiconductor inspection market.  Hartanah Kenyalang Bhd was also highlighted, with its RM851 million order book equivalent to about 6.8 times FY25 revenue and potentially positioning it to benefit from infrastructure-related initiatives in East Malaysia under Budget 2027.

title: Mahkamah Tinggi kekal keputusan timbang tara anugerah RM77 juta kepada SUJV
body: Kuala Lumpur: Mahkamah Tinggi mengekalkan keputusan Tribunal Timbang Tara menganugerahkan RM77 juta kepada kontraktor utama Menara Merdeka Maybank (sebelum ini dikenali Menara Merdeka 118). title: The greater isolation of lesser Israel
body: Vijay Prashad When Benjamin Netanyahu rose to address the UN General Assembly on 24 September, the rows of empty seats spoke before he did. Diplomats walked out, while others stayed away from the outset. News reports citing an Israeli tally put the number of delegations absent or departing at 77. This was not a recorded UN vote, nor did all 77 stage a coordinated walkout. Yet the image of an Israeli prime minister speaking to a depleted chamber captured a real political fact: the destruction of Gaza and the consolidation of occupation have made Israel increasingly isolated across much of the world. The diplomats who stayed away or who walked out were overwhelmingly drawn from Africa, Asia, the Arab world and Latin America, although European states including Spain and Ireland boycotted the address. Brazil and South Africa did not show up, while Indonesia, Pakistan, Senegal, Sudan and Turkey stayed away. The empty seats did not mean that each of these countries stayed away for the same reason. However, it is essential to point out that for many of them, Palestine is not a distant diplomatic file but a liberation project akin to their own struggles against colonial rule and for sovereignty. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member They refused to listen to Netanyahu as the occupation, apartheid, genocide and expropriation were happening in plain sight. The rebuke came at the correct time. In his address, Netanyahu rejected all genocide allegations. However, in June 2026, a UN independent commission said that Israeli authorities and forces continued to commit genocide and other atrocity crimes, specifically in their treatment of Palestinian children. This commission had previously concluded in 2025 that Israel was committing a genocide. These are findings of a UN investigative body, not a final judgment in the genocide case before the International Court of Justice. The difference between a commission’s findings and a court’s eventual ruling matters legally, but it does not make the evidence of Israeli violence and Palestinian suffering disappear. Permanent genocide The 10 October 2025 ceasefire did not bring an end to the genocide or the suffering. UN humanitarian reporting in September 2026 describes continuing deaths, restricted access to essential supplies, mass displacement and a landscape of shattered homes and public services. Just before the report was published, in Tal al-Hawa on 16 September, a building damaged by Israeli attacks collapsed and killed at least 21 people, including eight children. “Israeli air strikes, shelling, drone attacks and ground operations have continued,” the UN investigators write, “and Palestinian casualties continue to mount. “Around two-thirds of Gaza remains inaccessible or subject to severe access restrictions, leaving Palestinian civilians confined to overcrowded and insecure areas.” Jaco Cilliers, the United Nations Development Programme’s special representative in Gaza, told Seham Tantesh: “The estimate of the total rubble in Gaza is 61 million tonnes. It is approximately 20 times the amount of rubble generated in all wars across the world over the last 18 years.” The global outrage at the genocide is not only retrospective, directed at the devastation of the years before the ceasefire. It responds to a present in which Palestinians remain exposed to violence, deprivation and political subjugation. Gaza is only one of three parts of the occupied Palestinian territory, the other two parts being East Jerusalem and the West Bank. In July 2024, the International Court of Justice held in an advisory opinion that Israel’s continued presence in the occupied territory was unlawful and that the Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the seizures of buildings and land in East Jerusalem violated international law. Drawing on this opinion, the UN General Assembly demanded that Israel end its unlawful presence within a year. As if to snub the UN, in April 2025 Israel established a new enforcement unit within its land authority to identify ‘illegal’ Palestinian construction in the West Bank with the intent of demolishing them and building more illegal settlements. The UN secretary general published his report in September 2025, which showed that nothing had changed a year after the UN General Assembly’s deadline passed. The gap between international legal principle and the facts imposed on the ground has become impossible to disguise with appeals to an indefinitely postponed peace process. Profits from apartheid On 25 September, the UN human rights office updated its database of businesses engaged specific activities connected to Israel’s illegal settlements. Its latest report, A/HRC/63/20, lists 214 enterprises based in 11 countries, compared with 158 in the 2025 edition. The UN says the list is limited to activities identified under its Human Rights Council mandate, and so it is not a catalogue of every company with commercial links to Israel, nor a judicial finding that each listed firm has committed a crime. Its purpose is to make the economic machinery of the settlements visible, which had been done in 2025 in the report by Francesca Albanese ‘From economy of occupation to economy of genocide. Report of the special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967’. These reports show that the settler machinery reaches well beyond the settler movement itself to companies that provide construction, finance, telecoms, services and markets. Through the work of these companies the ‘temporary’ nature of the settlements is made permanent. The database supplies a practical and concrete list for tracing the relationships between settlers and these companies and asks governments and investors what they will do about these relationships. Most listed enterprises are Israeli, but foreign firms included businesses that are mostly headquartered in the US and several European countries. These governments that invoke a ‘rules-based order’ cannot treat their own companies’ participation in such a blatantly unlawful settlement economy as an incidental commercial matter. The facts established in the list should now put additional pressure on states (in particular, Canada, France and the UK) whose public opposition to settlements is contradicted by the continuation of their firms in the settlement economy. The UN database does not automatically prescribe sanctions against named companies, but it does make indifference harder to defend. Governments can investigate listed activities, exclude settlement products and services from preferential treatment, examine public contracts and require firms to end involvement that sustains occupation. These measures would connect the principles proclaimed at the UN to the economic system that keeps settlements viable. Incomplete isolation Israel’s diplomatic isolation is substantial but incomplete. Empty seats did not halt the violence or dismantle a single settlement, while strong statements in New York can coexist with trade, arms transfers and investments that sustain the status quo. The US and other powerful partners still possess the means to shield Israel from consequences, even as opposition grows in the UN General Assembly. For Palestinians, symbolic rejection is meaningful only if it develops into sustained pressure for protection, accountability, an end to unlawful occupation, and the exercise of self-determination. The scene at the General Assembly and the publication of the business database belong in the same story. One revealed a loss of political consent, while the other mapped some of the economic relationships that allow it to survive. The overwhelming presence of Global South countries among those absent or departing reflects a widening refusal to accept mass Palestinian suffering as the price of geopolitical alliance. The task now is to give that refusal material force. A world that turns its back on Netanyahu’s defence of the occupation must also withdraw the contracts, investments and diplomatic cover through which occupation is made to endure. – Globetrotter Vijay Prashad is an Indian historian and journalist. He is the author of 40 books, including Washington Bullets, Red Star Over the Third World, The Darker Nations: A People’s History of the Third World, The Poorer Nations: A Possible History of the Global South, and How the International Monetary Fund Suffocates Africa, written with Grieve Chelwa. He is the executive director of Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, the chief correspondent for Globetrotter, and the chief editor of LeftWord Books (New Delhi). He also appeared in the films Shadow World (2016) and Two Meetings (2017). The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: DNB Raih Pembiayaan Islamik RM5.2 Bilion, MoF Inc Bersedia Lepas Pegangan Saham Biasa
body: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) berjaya memperoleh pembiayaan bertempoh Islamik bersama berjumlah RM5.2 bilion. Langkah ini memperkukuh kedudukan kewangan syarikat tatkala Malaysia melangkah ke fasa seterusnya dalam pelaksanaan rangka kerja dwi-rangkaian 5G. Kemudahan pembiayaan ini menyediakan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang baharu bagi DNB seiring persiapannya beroperasi di bawah model pemilikan yang diterajui sepenuhnya oleh pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alih (MNO). Peralihan Pemilikan dan Penstrukturan Saham Penyusunan pembiayaan ini hadir ketika Menteri Kewangan (Diperbadankan) atau MoF Inc bersedia untuk melepaskan pegangan saham biasanya dalam DNB. Peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata antara tiga syarikat telekomunikasi utama—CelcomDigi, Maxis Broadband, dan YTL Power International—dijangka selesai pada awal suku keempat tahun 2026. Walau bagaimanapun, MoF Inc akan mengekalkan ‘saham khas’ dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan nasional serta mengawal selia perkara strategik negara. Struktur pemegang saham DNB menyaksikan perubahan ketara dalam beberapa tahun kebelakangan ini: - Telekom Malaysia (TM): Menamatkan penyertaan ekuiti pada tahun 2023. - U Mobile: Melepaskan pegangan sahamnya pada tahun 2025 untuk menumpukan usaha membangunkan rangkaian 5G kedua Malaysia. - Pemegang Saham Semasa: CelcomDigi (melalui Infranation Sdn Bhd), Maxis Broadband, dan YTL Power International (syarikat induk kepada pengendali Yes 5G, YTL Communications). Antara Kemudahan Perkongsian Terbesar Syarikat Tidak Tersenarai Menurut DNB, pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini tersenarai antara fasiliti pinjaman berkongsi terbesar yang pernah diatur bagi sebuah syarikat tidak tersenarai di Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank bertindak sebagai Pengatur Utama Mandat, Pengendali Tempahan, dan Pengatur Penyelaras. Manakala AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank, serta United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) bertindak sebagai Pengatur Utama Mandat Bersama. Kemudahan baharu ini merangkumi pembiayaan semula Kemudahan Kredit Pusingan Jaminan Kerajaan DNB yang telah tamat tempoh pada 29 September 2026. Ia membentuk struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang yang mampan bagi menyokong pelaburan rangkaian dan pertumbuhan masa hadapan DNB. Menerusi kenyataan berasingan oleh CelcomDigi, pembiayaan ini dijangka mengurangkan keperluan suntikan dana ekuiti tambahan daripada pemegang saham MNO berdasarkan komitmen kawal selia dan keperluan dana semasa. Situasi ini membolehkan syarikat-syarikat telekomunikasi memfokuskan usaha terhadap peningkatan kecekapan dan prestasi operasi rangkaian 5G. Pegangan Spektrum 240MHz Melalui Penyerahan Hak Jangka Panjang Perkembangan pembiayaan ini disusuli dengan penerimaan peruntukan penuh 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3GHz hingga 3.4GHz oleh DNB, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan pegangan spektrum syarikat meningkat kepada 240MHz. Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) turut menukar keseluruhan pegangan spektrum DNB kepada Penyerahan Hak Spektrum (Spectrum Assignment) berkuat kuasa 1 Oktober 2026. Sebelum ini, DNB telah menerima peruntukan tambahan 100MHz pada Julai 2026, memberikannya 200MHz spektrum jalur pertengahan berturutan (contiguous mid-band spectrum) dalam julat 3.3GHz hingga 3.5GHz. Peruntukan tambahan tersebut tersedia susulan pengunduran U Mobile daripada rangkaian DNB untuk melancarkan rangkaian 5G sendiri. Penyerahan hak spektrum bagi tempoh 15 tahun ini menawarkan kepastian jangka panjang kepada CelcomDigi dan rakan kongsi lain bagi merancang pelaburan infrastruktur. DNB menegaskan bahawa perluasan spektrum ini akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan, dan prestasi rangkaian, di samping menyokong integrasi teknologi lanjutan seperti: - Massive MIMO: Teknologi antena berskala besar untuk memperluas kapasiti transmisi data serentak. - Carrier Aggregation: Penggabungan beberapa jalur frekuensi bagi mencapai kelajuan sambungan lebih tinggi. - 5G Advanced & Keupayaan Pacuan AI: Peningkatan seni bina rangkaian generasi seterusnya yang dipacu kecerdasan buatan. CelcomDigi Manfaatkan Aset dan Pengalaman Rangkaian Melalui peralihan pemilikan ini, CelcomDigi menyatakan komitmennya untuk memanfaatkan aset rangkaian di seluruh negara serta pengalaman telekomunikasi melebihi 30 tahun bagi memacu fasa pembangunan DNB seterusnya. Sinergi antara infrastruktur, tapak menara, dan keupayaan sedia ada CelcomDigi dengan rangkaian DNB dijangka membantu meningkatkan kecekapan kos, meluaskan liputan, mempercepat pelaksanaan 5G dalam bangunan (indoor 5G deployment), memperkukuh penyelesaian bangunan tertutup, serta memaksimumkan utilisasi spektrum.

title: Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card: Everything you need to know before applying
body: Maybank has officially introduced its limited edition Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card in Malaysia. With initial physical branch allocations selling out rapidly across the country, fans looking to secure the card should now stand by for the official Maybank2u online rollout on 28 September 2026. What is the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? The card is an exclusive limited edition Visa debit card released in collaboration with Visa for the BTS World Tour Arirang. It links directly to any existing or new Maybank current or savings account, including popular options like a standard Savings Account i. Maybank has capped total nationwide issuance to 200,000 cards. Following the instant sell out of physical branch quotas, remaining card stock will be made available strictly through online applications. Additional features compared to a standard Maybank debit card While core banking functions mirror standard Maybank debit cards, the BTS edition includes several exclusive perks and modern payment integrations. Cardholders can add the Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card to Apple Pay and Samsung Wallet. This allows users to make contactless mobile payments directly from an iPhone, Apple Watch, or compatible Samsung Galaxy device without needing the physical card on hand. Beyond mobile wallet support and limited edition artwork, getting the card grants an immediate advantage in Maybank and Visa’s official concert ticket giveaway. While standard debit cardholders must accumulate spending to qualify, obtaining this limited edition card automatically awards an entry into the prize draw. In terms of banking capabilities, the card operates on the Visa network with smart chip security, contactless highway toll support, and standard fee structures, including the standard RM12 replacement fee. How to win BTS World Tour Arirang concert tickets in Kuala Lumpur Maybank and Visa are running a contest from 23 September 2026 until 1 November 2026, offering cardholders a chance to win pairs of tickets to the BTS World Tour Arirang concert at National Stadium Bukit Jalil on 12 December 2026. To participate, cardholders must first register by sending an SMS with the word BTS to the number 66628, or register through the dedicated Maybank2u promotion page. Once registered, users can earn entries through multiple qualifying actions: - Automatic entry: Successfully applying for or replacing an existing card with the limited edition BTS debit card awards one automatic entry. - Cumulative spending: Every cumulative RM400 spent on eligible retail transactions using any Maybank Visa debit card during the campaign period earns one entry. - Additional spending: Every subsequent RM400 spent yields additional entries to boost winning chances. Transactions involving eWallet top ups, government payments, and charity donations are excluded from eligible spend. Winners will be selected through Maybank’s randomiser system, with each cardmember eligible to win a maximum of one pair of tickets. How to apply for the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? With physical branch allocations fully exhausted, all remaining card requests must be submitted online when portal access opens on 28 September 2026. Existing Maybank customers Existing Maybank debit cardholders do not need to visit a branch or collect cards in person. You can request a card replacement online via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. To place an order, log in to Maybank2u on the web, navigate to Settings, select Cards, go to Manage Debit Cards, and click Replace or Renew Card. Select the BTS card, enter your mailing address, and confirm the request using Secure2u or SMS TAC. The card will be delivered directly to your home address for a standard RM12 replacement fee. Delivery times may exceed thirty days during periods of high demand. If card allocations run out completely before your request processes, Maybank will issue a full refund of the replacement fee. Non-Maybank customers If you do not currently hold a Maybank account, you cannot directly order a card replacement online as a first time applicant. New customers must first open an account with Maybank. You can set up an account online through the MAE app or visit any Maybank branch with your MyKad or passport and a standard RM250 deposit, or RM50 with an employment letter. Once your account is active and registered on Maybank2u, you can stand by to request the BTS debit card replacement via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. Transaction limits and security settings The card comes with a default daily purchase limit of RM3,000, which can be increased up to RM10,000 via Maybank2u or adjusted at any Maybank ATM. Each card carries a validity period of seven years from issuance. Cardholders planning to use the card for online shopping or overseas ATM cash withdrawals must manually activate ecommerce and overseas transaction features inside Maybank2u prior to making transactions.

title: JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis | Sinar Harian
body: JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis KUALA LUMPUR - Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM) menyasarkan pelantikan 24,000 Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO) menjelang tahun 2030 sebagai langkah perkukuh kawal selia serta aspek keselamatan kebakaran di premis. Ini sekali gus menjadi kompenan penting dalam penubuhan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK). Ketua Pengarah Bomba, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, bagi pelantikan FSM, jumlahnya dijangka seramai 6,000 orang, manakala pelantikan FSO seramai 18,000 orang. Menurutnya, JBPM melihat sasaran ini sebagai satu keperluan strategik dan setakat ini seramai 498 lantikan telah dibuat membabitkan 174 peserta FSM dan 324 peserta FSO. "Ini merupakan sebahagian daripada keperluan untuk mematuhi Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba 1988 (Pindaan 2025) yang mensyaratkan bagi mana-mana premis yang dikenakan penguatkuasaan Perakuan Bomba perlu menubuhkan OKK. "OKK itu perlu ada jumlah yang minimum untuk dilantik dan dalam kalangan itu perlu ada seorang FSM dan tiga orang FSO," katanya dalam sidang akhbar selepas Majlis Pelancaran FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini pada Selasa. Tambahnya, sebagai persediaan ke arah OKK, JBPM telah melaksanakan pelbagai program libat urus bersama pihak berkepentingan. Katanya, Malaysia mempunyai sekitar 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan dengan profil dan tahap risiko keselamatan kebakaran yang berbeza. "Asasnya ialah bangunan yang telah kita kategorikan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba," ujarnya. Jelas beliau, penguatkuasaan OKK secara penuh ini dijadualkan bermula 1 April 2027 sekali gus memberikan tempoh persediaan kepada pihak industri untuk membangunkan kompetensi, struktur organisasi dan tahap pematuhan yang diperlukan. "FSM dan FSO tidak akan mengambil alih peranan JBPM, tetapi melengkapkan ekosistem keselamatan kebakaran melalui pengurusan risiko secara berterusan di peringkat premis," ujarnya. Nor Hisham berkata, salah satu fungsi FSM ialah mengurangkan beban kepada penguatkuasaan berkaitan Perakuan Bomba. "Kalau pada amalan semasa ini berdasarkan prosedur-prosedur semasa kita periksa setiap tahun untuk kita keluarkan Sijil Perakuan Bomba. Tetapi di masa hadapan, tempoh itu akan kita jarakkan lagi. "Laporan pemeriksaan akan disediakan oleh FSM sebelum kita menilai dan membuat pembaharuan," ujarnya. Nor Hisham sebelum itu menyerahkan sijil perakuan kepada kumpulan pertama FSM serta FSO yang memenuhi syarat kelayakan ditetapkan. Muat turun aplikasi Sinar Harian. Klik di sini!

title: FBM KLCI Susut 15 Mata, Saham Bank & Utiliti Tekan Pasaran
body: Bursa Malaysia meneruskan penurunan pada tengah hari Khamis apabila tekanan jualan kembali mendominasi pasaran, selari dengan prestasi bercampur pasaran global ketika kenaikan hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat terus mengehadkan sentimen risiko. Pada 12:30 tengah hari, FBM KLCI susut 15.36 mata kepada 1,635.81 berbanding 1,651.17 pada penutupan Rabu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87 sebelum bergerak antara 1,634.39 hingga 1,649.87 sepanjang sesi pagi. Kaunter Rugi Mendominasi Pasaran Sentimen keseluruhan kekal lemah apabila 583 kaunter mencatat penurunan berbanding 305 kaunter yang meningkat. Sebanyak 464 kaunter tidak berubah, manakala 1,421 kaunter tidak didagangkan dan 12 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan mencapai 1.65 bilion saham bernilai RM1.18 bilion. Saham Bank Dan Tenaga Terus Tertekan Dalam kalangan saham berwajaran tinggi, Maybank dan Tenaga Nasional masing-masing susut 6 sen kepada RM9.93 dan RM12.90. Public Bank pula turun 4 sen kepada RM4.66, manakala CIMB berkurang 5 sen kepada RM7.74. IHH Healthcare turut susut 19 sen kepada RM7.64. Tekanan daripada kaunter berkapitalisasi besar ini menjadi antara faktor yang mengekang FBM KLCI pada sesi tengah hari. Data Pekerjaan AS Jadi Perhatian Apex Securities berkata sentimen pasaran turut terjejas selepas pengambilan pekerja sektor swasta AS meningkat lebih daripada jangkaan, dengan 90,000 pekerjaan ditambah pada September. Perkembangan tersebut mengimbangi kelegaan daripada data inflasi teras Personal Consumption Expenditures yang lebih rendah. Pelabur kini menunggu laporan Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) AS pada Jumaat bagi mendapatkan petunjuk baharu mengenai hala tuju dasar Rizab Persekutuan AS. Pada masa sama, perkembangan rundingan Amerika Syarikat dan Iran serta pergerakan harga minyak turut menjadi perhatian pasaran. Zetrix AI Antara Kaunter Aktif Dalam dagangan aktif, Zetrix AI dan V.S Industry masing-masing meningkat setengah sen kepada 16.5 sen dan 28.5 sen. Jaks Resources pula susut setengah sen kepada 20 sen, manakala saham baharu ACE Market, GB Bond, turun 2.5 sen kepada 22.5 sen. Dagang Nexchange pula kembali mengukuh 1.5 sen kepada 50 sen. MPI Catat Kenaikan Terbesar Bagi kaunter untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) menjadi antara yang mencatat kenaikan terbesar dengan menambah RM1.26 kepada RM41.66. MI Technovation pula meningkat 13 sen kepada RM5.33, diikuti Ta Ann yang naik 12 sen kepada RM5.92. Malayan Cement dan Genting Plantations masing-masing meningkat 11 sen dan 10 sen kepada RM5.56 dan RM5.63. KLK Antara Kaunter Paling Susut Sementara itu, Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) mengetuai senarai kaunter rugi dengan susut 76 sen kepada RM21.44. Allianz Malaysia pula turun 62 sen kepada RM21, manakala Fraser & Neave, Hong Leong Industries dan Batu Kawan masing-masing berkurang 42 sen kepada RM21.32, RM16.04 dan RM20.10. Kebanyakan Indeks Dalam Zon Merah Di papan indeks, FBM Mid 70 susut 87.65 mata kepada 17,487.02, manakala FBM Emas turun 94.18 mata kepada 12,197.83. FBM Top 100 pula berkurang 99 mata kepada 11,985.44, manakala FBM Emas Shariah susut 87.69 mata kepada 12,088.65. FBM ACE turut turun 31.4 mata kepada 5,503.14.
